docs.title: Platform execution pathways
docs.text:
SIMANFOR is designed to accommodate diverse technical profiles, from students and forest practitioners seeking to assess a single silvicultural prescription, to researchers processing thousands of inventory plots in high-performance computing environments.

To address these varying needs, three interaction pathways with the platform exist. This guide outlines each alternative, clarifies the current operational status of each service, and provides a decision matrix to help you select the most suitable pathway.

docs.title: Table of contents
docs.text:
• Access decision tree
  • Web platform: the primary and recommended pathway
  • Docker container
  • Python simulator and new model development
  • Decision matrix by user profile
  • Recommended next steps

docs.title: Access decision tree
docs.text: The following diagram summarizes the recommended interaction pathway based on operational requirements and data volume:

docs.title: Web platform: the primary and recommended pathway
docs.text: The web platform available at simanfor.es is the official, primary, and recommended pathway for the vast majority of users (forest managers, environmental consultants, educators, and students).

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Cloud service with zero installation: Runs directly in any modern web browser (Firefox, Chrome, Edge, Safari). Requires no local software installation, programming environment configuration, or operating system dependency management.
  • Open and free access: Available freely without licensing fees. Only requires registering a user account to privately store inventories, scenarios, and outputs.
  • Guided visual interface: Allows users to upload inventory files in Excel using standardized templates, select models from the official catalog, define thinning interventions step by step, and inspect diagnostic reports.
  • Direct export: Simulation results are compiled into downloadable Excel workbooks organized by stand-level trajectories, residual inventory tables, and commercial timber assessments.

Recommended starting pathway

If you are taking your first steps with SIMANFOR, completing an academic assignment, or drafting a forest management plan for a specific stand or property, the web platform covers 100% of your computational requirements without technical friction. See the Web platform user guide for a comprehensive walkthrough.

docs.title: Docker container
docs.text: Historically, SIMANFOR provided public Docker container images to enable local offline execution on standalone machines.

docs.title: Current operational status
docs.text:
Public Docker container images for external users are temporarily suspended due to technical review and infrastructure maintenance.

  • Technical rationale: The simulator core and model architecture have undergone significant refactoring toward a Single Source of Truth (SSOT) architecture and numerical performance optimizations. Earlier container images are being redesigned to ensure exact synchronization with the latest verified versions of all biometric models.
  • Current recommendation: While this update is completed, all users needing to run simulations should use the cloud-based web platform (simanfor.es), which features the latest verified versions of the entire model catalog.
  • Future availability: Once the verification of the lightweight updated images is complete, a comprehensive local deployment guide will be published in this section.

Docker service under update

The Docker section of the user documentation remains under maintenance. The cloud platform at simanfor.es is fully operational and serves as the direct, verified alternative.

docs.title: Python simulator and new model development
docs.text: For research groups, forest modelers, and advanced data scientists requiring capabilities beyond the graphical interface, the SIMANFOR computational engine is implemented as a modular tool in Python.

docs.title: Specialized use cases
docs.text:
• Large-scale batch simulations: Systematic processing of thousands of Spanish National Forest Inventory (NFI) plots or extensive regional biometric databases.
  • High-performance computing (HPC): Distributed simulation deployments on high-performance servers.
  • Integration into analytical pipelines: Programmatic connection of the simulator with R or Python workflows for statistical modeling, multi-objective optimization, or advanced visualization.
  • Model calibration and integration: Implementation of new growth functions, allometric relationships, or parameters for species and regions not yet covered in the catalog.

docs.title: Access protocol and scientific collaboration
docs.text:
Because these environments require close coordination with the SIMANFOR development team, access to the advanced simulator scripts and model integration is managed through scientific or technical collaboration agreements.

If your institution, research project, or case study requires this deployment mode, please contact the team directly at simanfor.forest@uva.es, including: 1. The research scope and project objectives. 2. The estimated volume of inventories and scenarios to be processed. 3. The biometric equations or models you wish to calibrate or test within the simulator.

Pedagogical recommendation

docs.title: Recommended learning pathways
docs.text:
Depending on your objectives and background, we suggest following one of these structured tracks:

  • Quick-start track (for new users and students): Videos in Block 1 $\rightarrow$ Videos in Block 2. In under 30 minutes, you will learn how to set up an account, upload an inventory, run a projection, and download the output Excel workbook.
  • Applied silviculture track (for forest managers and practitioners): Videos in Block 2 $\rightarrow$ Block 3 $\rightarrow$ Block 4. Designed to master model selection, thinning from below/above design, and crop tree protection.
  • Research and data analysis track (for researchers and consultants): Videos in Block 4 $\rightarrow$ Block 5. Focused on fine-grained scenario diagnosis and automated comparative reporting using R scripts.

docs.title: 3.1. Stand-level model simulations
docs.text:
• Objective: Run simulations when tree-level data are unavailable, relying on aggregate plot metrics.
  • Key content: Ingesting simplified stand inventories ($N$, $G$, $Ho$, age), stand-level model specificities, and recommended use cases.

docs.title: 3.2. Individual-tree model simulations for pure stands
docs.text:
• Objective: Simulate monospecific stands with single-tree resolution (e.g., Pinus sylvestris or Pinus pinaster).
  • Key content: Diameter distribution dynamics, distance-independent inter-tree competition ($BAL$, $d/dg$), and merchantable log assortments.

docs.title: 3.3. Individual-tree model simulations for mixed stands
docs.text:
• Objective: Model the growth dynamics and competition between two or more coexisting species in a shared stand.
  • Key content: Supported species combinations (e.g., Scots pine and sessile oak in the Central Mountain Range), mixing proportions, and differential growth responses.

docs.title: 3.4. Static model simulations
docs.text:
• Objective: Utilize SIMANFOR as a static stand volume calculator and stock estimator at measurement time ($t = 0$).
  • Key content: Official tariff equations, biomass fraction calculations, and stock estimation for management inventories.

docs.text: Detailed guidance for modeling realistic silvicultural interventions and troubleshooting complex scenarios.

docs.title: 4.1. Applying thinnings and cuttings in SIMANFOR
docs.text:
• Objective: Configure tree removal interventions along a scenario timeline.
  • Key content: Thinning type selection (from below, from above, systematic), metric selection ($N$, $G$, or $V$), and percentage removal intensity.

docs.title: 4.2. Species-selective cuttings in mixed stands
docs.text:
• Objective: Modulate species composition by targeting specific species in mixed stands.
  • Key content: Differential prescriptions applied exclusively to one species while maintaining the companion canopy intact.

docs.title: 4.3. Cuttings with crop trees
docs.text:
• Objective: Model precision silviculture by designating and protecting high-value target trees.
  • Key content: Selecting and marking target trees with superior stem form or vigor, securing their retention, and removing direct competitors.

docs.title: 4.4. Applying the same scenario across plots of different ages
docs.text:
• Objective: Manage heterogeneous plot collections or uneven-aged stands using unified decision rules.
  • Key content: Defining conditional scenarios and synchronized projection steps for regional or estate-scale inventories.

docs.title: 4.5. Frequent scenario errors and debugging
docs.text:
• Objective: Diagnose and resolve the most common issues triggering execution warnings or failures.
  • Key content: Time intervals incompatible with model biological steps, excessive harvests reducing residual density below biological thresholds, and server error code interpretation.

docs.title: Block 5: Advanced results analysis
docs.text: Techniques to process, analyze, and present simulation outputs with high analytical rigor.

docs.title: Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
docs.text: This section gathers direct answers and practical solutions to the most common questions raised by forest managers, researchers, and students when using SIMANFOR. Questions are organized across five thematic areas to facilitate quick navigation.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
• General and access questions
  • Inventories and data preparation
  • Forest models and parameterization
  • Silvicultural scenarios and interventions
  • Troubleshooting and common issues

docs.title: Is SIMANFOR a free tool?
docs.text: Yes. SIMANFOR is free of charge for education, scientific research, technical consulting, and public or private forest management, with no licensing fees or restrictions on the number of simulations.

docs.title: Do I need to install any software on my computer?
docs.text: No. The primary access pathway runs entirely in the cloud at simanfor.es. You only need a standard web browser (Firefox, Chrome, Edge, or Safari) and an internet connection. Calculations are processed on University of Valladolid servers.

docs.title: In which languages are the web platform and the simulator available?
docs.text:
• Web platform (simanfor.es): The user interface allows selecting different languages for navigating menus and configuration windows.
  • Simulator engine and Excel outputs: The core biometric computation engine and result workbooks are formally verified and supported in Spanish and English.
  • Technical documentation: The official portal is maintained synchronously in both languages (ES / EN).

docs.title: How should I cite SIMANFOR in a report or scientific publication?
docs.text:
The general reference paper to cite formally is:

Bravo, F., Ordóñez, C., Vázquez-Veloso, A., and Michalakopoulos, S. (2025). SIMANFOR cloud Decision Support System: Structure, content, and applications. Ecological Modelling, 499, 110912. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2024.110912

In addition, we recommend citing the specific growth model paper used in your simulation, whose full bibliographic references can be found in its respective technical sheet in the Models section.

docs.title: Why does the simulator reject common species names?
docs.text:
SIMANFOR requires identifying tree species using either their scientific Latin name (e.g., Pinus sylvestris, Quercus pyrenaica) or their official Spanish National Forest Inventory numerical code (e.g., 21 for Pinus sylvestris, 43 for Quercus pyrenaica).

Common vernacular names vary substantially across regions, countries, and dialects (pino albar, Scots pine, pino silvestre, pino de Valsaín), which would introduce biological ambiguities into equation assignment.

docs.title: What happens if tree heights are missing from my individual-tree inventory?
docs.text: You do not need to discard the plot. In tree-by-tree inventories where height was measured only on a representative sample of trees, SIMANFOR automatically applies local or generalized height-diameter ($h/d$) submodels calibrated for each species and region, imputing the heights of the remaining stems.

docs.title: What is the expansion factor (expan) and why is it mandatory?
docs.text:
The expansion factor represents the number of trees per hectare represented by each sampled tree in the inventory plot. It depends directly on the sampling design: * Fixed-radius plots ($r$): $\text{expan} = \frac{10000}{\pi \cdot r^2}$. For example, in a 15 m circular plot ($706.86\text{ m}^2$), each measured tree has an $\text{expan} \approx 14.15\text{ trees/ha}$. * Concentric NFI plots: The expansion factor varies depending on the concentric circle radius in which the tree was measured according to its diameter class (nested circular subplots with radii of 5 m, 10 m, 15 m, or 25 m).

The simulator requires expan to accurately scale individual-tree attributes to per-hectare stand values ($N$, $G$, $V$, biomass, and carbon).

docs.title: What is the difference between the Parcelas / Plots sheet and the PiesMayores / Trees sheet?
docs.text: In SIMANFOR Excel templates: * Parcelas (or Plots) sheet: Each row defines a plot or stand with geographic identifiers and global variables (stand age, slope, site index, etc.). * PiesMayores (or Trees) sheet: Each row describes an individual tree measured in the field, specifying its species, diameter at breast height (dbh), height (h), and expansion factor (expan). * Critical rule: The identifiers ID_Inventario and ID_parcela must match exactly between both sheets so that the computation engine can link trees to their corresponding stand.

docs.title: How do I choose the right forest model for my stand?
docs.text:
To select the appropriate model from the SIMANFOR catalog, evaluate four biometric criteria: 1. Species composition: Is the stand pure (single species) or mixed? 2. Input data resolution: If you have tree-by-tree data, select an individual-tree model. If you only have aggregate stand metrics ($N$, $G$, $Ho$, age), choose a stand-level model. 3. Geographic scope and provenance: Many models feature regional parameterizations (e.g., coastal Galicia vs. inland Galicia vs. Central Mountain Range). 4. Input data requirements: Verify that your inventory contains all variables required by the selected model.

You can inspect the detailed specifications of each model in the model technical sheets.

docs.title: Why shouldn't the time step (time) of a projection be modified arbitrarily?
docs.text:
Each dynamic growth model was scientifically calibrated using permanent plots or repeated inventories over a specific biological time interval (typically 5- or 10-year periods).

Modifying this interval to force annual projections or non-validated projection intervals can introduce numerical biases into mortality functions or nonlinear diameter and height growth rates. Always follow the recommended step indicated in the model technical sheet.

docs.title: Can I incorporate my own model into the simulator?
docs.text: Yes. SIMANFOR is a collaborative open project receptive to integrating new forestry equations. If you have developed or calibrated a growth model, allometric relationships, or mortality functions for species or regions not yet covered, contact the team at simanfor.forest@uva.es to explore implementation in the simulator.

docs.title: What is the practical difference between thinning from below and thinning from above?
docs.text:
• Thinning from below: Trees from the dominated stratum—namely, trees with smaller diameter at breast height—are preferentially harvested. This reduces competition-induced mortality and concentrates resources on the dominant stratum without drastically modifying dominant height ($Ho$).
  • Thinning from above: Selected trees from codominant and dominant strata competing directly with target crop trees—namely, trees with larger diameter at breast height—are harvested. This promotes crown expansion in crop trees and typically provides higher immediate income from sawlog sales.

docs.title: Why doesn't the simulator allow running a harvest directly without an initial projection?
docs.text: The calculation engine must initialize all biological vigor variables, inter-tree competition metrics, and allometric coefficients from raw inventory data. The first projection step establishes model internal consistency before mathematical selection and biomass extraction rules can be evaluated.

docs.title: Why can't I find options for pruning, fertilization, or cork stripping?
docs.text:
Currently, SIMANFOR only implements tree removal operations (thinnings and cleanings).

In quantitative silviculture, implementing a technical intervention requires an empirically validated mathematical model that quantifies its direct effect on radial growth, allometry, and tree survival. As the scientific community develops and validates these functions, they will be incorporated into the platform.

docs.title: Why does the web simulation return an empty or 0-byte ZIP file?
docs.text:
In many cases, this simply occurs because the server has not yet finished calculations and the user attempts downloading the file prematurely. If this happens, it is recommended to refresh the page (F5), check the simulation status or re-launch the run, and wait until the platform generates and delivers the ZIP file with the results.

If after waiting the file remains empty, it usually indicates that the calculation engine has detected a structural inconsistency in the inventory or scenario and aborted execution preventively. The most frequent causes are: 1. Incorrect or non-standard column headers in Excel sheets (e.g., hidden spaces or unrecognized capitalization). 2. Trees in the PiesMayores / Trees sheet whose ID_Inventario or ID_parcela identifiers do not match those in the Parcelas / Plots sheet. 3. Botanical species not supported by the selected forest model. 4. A scenario with harvest intensities attempting to extract more than 100% of standing stock.

Review your file structure against the official templates in the Inventories section.

docs.title: Why does my scenario remain in WAITING status?
docs.text: The WAITING status indicates that your simulation is queued on the server. If several simulations are running concurrently, it may take a few minutes. If it does not advance after a reasonable period, refresh the page with F5. If it remains blocked, verify that your inventory does not contain thousands of plots exceeding web execution thresholds, or contact technical support.

docs.title: What is the difference between warnings and errors in the Diagnostico sheet?
docs.text: The SIMANFOR output workbook includes a dedicated quality control tab (Diagnostico): * Warnings: Point out advisory biometric or biological anomalies (e.g., a tree with an atypical height/diameter ratio or a plot whose density lies at the boundary of calibration data). The simulation continues successfully. * Fatal errors: Indicate severe mathematical inconsistencies preventing biological calculations (e.g., zero basal area, unsupported species, or missing mandatory data). The simulation stops to prevent erroneous output generation.

docs.title: Forest Growth Models in SIMANFOR
docs.text:
SIMANFOR integrates a diverse catalog of forest growth models to simulate stand development and evaluate silvicultural management alternatives (see harvest models).

Models are divided into two main growth categories plus a dedicated suite of silvicultural harvest models:

  1. Individual-tree models: Operate at the single-tree level, simulating tree growth, mortality probability, and ingrowth in a detailed manner, and computing plot attributes based on all individual trees present in the plot.
  2. Stand-level models: Operate at the aggregate plot or stand level, projecting variables such as tree density, basal area, total volume, and dominant height.
  3. Thinning models: Define tree extraction and harvesting according to silvicultural criteria (thinning from below, from above, systematic, by species, or with crop trees) for both tree and stand models.

docs.title: Individual-tree model calculation flow
docs.text: In individual-tree models, the simulation engine calculates biological processes considering individual trees and aggregated plot dynamics:

docs.title: Tree-level simulation phases:
docs.text:
1. Read initial inventory: Loads Plots (identifiers, site factors, etc.) and Trees (diameters, heights, species, and tree expansion factors).
  2. Initialization: Estimates missing inventory variables (heights, volumes, crown variables...) and computes aggregate plot metrics.
  3. Scenario simulation loop: According to user-defined silvicultural scenarios:
  4. Time projection: Evaluates individual survival, applies growth, incorporates new trees (ingrowth), and updates tree and plot metrics for the specified time period (this period must follow the recommendations of the model used).
  5. Harvest / Treatments: Removes selected trees (by size, species, or silvicultural rule) and updates remaining stand structure. For more details on thinning options, see the harvest models guide.
  6. Write output: Generates output tables with the state of the stand and trees at each simulation step.

docs.title: Stand-level model calculation flow
docs.text: Stand models simplify inventory data input, requiring only aggregate plot-level parameters without tree lists:

docs.title: Stand-level simulation phases:
docs.text:
1. Read initial inventory: Loads only the Plots sheet (age, density, basal area, dominant height as required).
  2. Initialization: Imputes required and missing initial stand attributes (volume, site index...).
  3. Scenario simulation loop:
  4. Time projection: Models aggregate stand growth and natural mortality curves, and updates plot variables for the established time period (this period must follow the recommendations of the model used).
  5. Harvest / Treatments: Applies direct reductions to density, basal area, or volume, updating plot metrics afterwards (see harvest models).
  6. Write output: Produces aggregated evolution tables.

docs.title: Harvest models configuration
docs.text:
Silvicultural interventions are defined in scenarios by selecting the appropriate harvest model, the thinning criterion (density, basal area, or volume), and the percentage intensity:

For full details on each harvest model, behavior in mixed stands, and parameter descriptions, see the harvest models and silvicultural treatments guide.

docs.title: Harvest models and silvicultural treatments
docs.text:
SIMANFOR includes a comprehensive suite of harvest and thinning models applicable to both individual-tree projections and stand-level (aggregate) models.

Silvicultural interventions are defined through the simulator's Scenarios, allowing users to evaluate the impacts of varying thinning intensities and regimes on each individual tree, the stand, and all calculated variables.

docs.title: Harvest models, criteria and thinning intensity
docs.text:
Every thinning intervention in SIMANFOR is defined by selecting a harvest model (apply thinning), associated with a thinning criterion (type) and a thinning intensity (percent):

  • Available harvest models (apply thinning):

    • For individual tree models:
      • Thinning from below
      • Thinning from above
      • Systematic thinning
      • Semi-systematic thinning (as a combination of the above, see details in Semi-systematic thinning)
      • Thinning (from below, from above or systematic) by species (mixed stands)
      • Thinning (systematic or from above) with future crop trees
      • Thinning (systematic or from above) with future crop trees by species (mixed stands)
    • For stand models:
      • Stand models harvests

  • Available thinning criteria (type):

    • Density: Number of trees per hectare (trees/ha).
    • Basal area: Stand basal area (m²/ha).
    • Volume: Over-bark stand volume (m³/ha).

  • Thinning intensity (percent): Percentage of the selected criterion to be removed during the intervention (value from 0 to 100 %).

docs.title: Minimum and maximum harvest age
docs.text:
Scenarios allow specifying an age range (min_age and max_age) to execute each harvest. This is particularly useful when simulating an inventory containing plots with different initial ages using the same scenario:

  • min_age: Minimum stand age required to execute the harvest (years).
  • max_age: Maximum stand age above which the harvest will not be applied (years).

Behavior outside the age range

If a plot's age is not within the range defined by min_age and max_age, the simulator will simply skip that harvest step for that plot and proceed with the rest of the simulation.

docs.title: Individual tree models harvests
docs.text: Individual tree harvest models operate by selecting and removing specific trees from the tree list according to their size (based on diameter at breast height dbh) and their species.

docs.title: Thinning from below
docs.text: Harvesting starts with the trees with the smallest diameter at breast height (dbh) in the plot and progresses upward through larger diameter classes until the target thinning percentage is fulfilled.

docs.title: Thinning from above
docs.text: Harvesting begins with the largest-diameter trees (dbh) in the plot and descends toward smaller diameter classes until reaching the specified intensity.

docs.title: Systematic thinning
docs.text: Harvesting is evenly distributed across all diameter classes, reducing the expansion factor (expan) of every tree in the plot by the same proportion.

docs.title: Semi-systematic thinning
docs.text: Although not programmed as a separate standalone model in SIMANFOR, it can be simulated by combining systematic and selective thinnings within the same scenario. For example, a semi-systematic thinning with a total intensity of 20 % can be simulated by applying a 10 % systematic thinning (representing line or rack opening) immediately followed by a 10 % thinning from below (representing selection among the remaining trees).

docs.title: Thinning (from below, from above or systematic) by species (mixed stands)
docs.text:
Allows targeting the harvest on a specific species in mixed stands using the following parameters:

  • species: Numerical species code according to the National Forest Inventory (IFN / SFNI, see the model documentation).
  • volume_target: Reference scope for the thinning intensity percentage:
    • Plot: The percentage is calculated relative to the total plot accumulation (cutting only trees of the target species).
    • Species: The percentage is calculated strictly relative to the standing stock of that target species within the plot.

docs.title: Thinning (systematic or from above) with future trees
docs.text:
• Additional parameter: preserve_trees (% of larger trees on which no action is to be taken, default is 15 %).
  • Behavior: A specified upper percentage of dominant or largest trees is protected (preserve_trees). Thinning is then executed immediately on the next largest diameter classes below the protected crop trees.

docs.title: Thinning (systematic or from above) with future trees by species (mixed stands)
docs.text: Combines the capabilities of the preceding thinning types, allowing users to configure target species (species), reference scope (volume_target), and percentage of crop trees to preserve (preserve_trees).

docs.title: Stand models harvests
docs.text:
In simulations using aggregate stand models, individual tree lists are not present, so harvests are systematic (with exceptions such as SILVES models, which include specific models to simulate thinnings from below and above). In these models, the configuration is as follows:

  • Harvest model: [masa] Corta sistemática ([stand] Systematic thinning)
  • Thinning criterion (type): densidad (density), area_basimetrica (basal_area) or volumen (volume)
  • Thinning intensity (percent): Percentage to be harvested (0 to 100 %)

• Description: Individual-tree growth model for Pinus nigra in Catalonia (Spain)
  • Target Species: Pinus nigra (code: 25)
  • Application Region: Catalonia (Girona, Lleida, Barcelona, and Tarragona; Spain)

docs.title: Technical characteristics
docs.text:
• Model Level: Individual tree
  • Allows Projection: Yes
  • Projection Time Step: 5 years
  • Notes: Individual tree model for Pinus nigra in Catalonia.

To view the step-by-step sequence of initialization, projection, and harvest, see the individual-tree model calculation flow diagram.

docs.title: Required variables
docs.text: To run this model in SIMANFOR, the initial inventory must include the following minimum data:

docs.title: Plot level (Plots sheet)
docs.text:
• Inventory and plot IDs
  • age
  • dominant height
  • slope, aspect and altitude (for fungi)

docs.title: Tree level (Trees sheet)
docs.text:
• Inventory, plot and tree IDs
  • species
  • expansion factor
  • dbh

docs.title: Modules and equations
docs.text:
Breakdown of simulated biological processes and their methodological references:

  • Reference forest growth model: Palahí & Grau (2003)
  • Site index / Stand productivity: Palahí & Grau (2003)
  • Growth: Palahí & Grau (2003)
  • Survival and/or mortality: Palahí & Grau (2003)
  • Ingrowth (trees of inventoriable size): Trasobares et al. (2004)
  • Stand Density Index (SDI) reference value: Aguirre et al. (2017)
  • Height-diameter relationship / height estimation: Palahí & Grau (2003)
  • Tree volume and taper: Rodríguez (2009), Rodríguez et al. (2015), MITECO (2025)
  • Biomass: Ruiz-Peinado et al. (2011)
  • Carbon content: Montero et al. (2005)
  • Non-wood forest products: Palahí et al. (2009)
  • Diversity indexes: Omoro et al. (2010), Simpson (1949), Ulanowicz (2001), Bray & Curtis (1957)
  • Structural and size indexes: Varga et al. (2005), Moreno-Fernández & others (2025), Barbeito (2009)

docs.title: Technical characteristics
docs.text:

  • Projection Time Step: 5 years

docs.title: General description
docs.text:
• Description: Distance-independent individual-tree growth model for pure stands in Spain
  • Target Species: Pinus sylvestris, Pinus uncinata, Pinus pinea, Pinus halepensis, Pinus nigra, Pinus pinaster, Pinus canariensis, Pinus radiata, Abies alba, Juniperus thurifera, Quercus robur, Quercus petraea, Quercus pyrenaica, Quercus faginea, Quercus ilex, Quercus suber, Populus nigra, Eucalyptus globulus, Eucalyptus camaldulensis, Fagus sylvatica, Castanea sativa, Quercus pubescens, Populus x canadensis, Betula alba (codes: 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 31, 38, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 58, 61, 62, 71, 72, 243, 258, 273)
  • Application Region: Spain

docs.title: Technical characteristics
docs.text:
• Model Level: Individual tree
  • Allows Projection: Yes
  • Projection Time Step: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 years
  • Notes: Projection age not defined, although periods over 10 years are not recommended.

To view the step-by-step sequence of initialization, projection, and harvest, see the individual-tree model calculation flow diagram.

docs.title: Interpretation of simulation outputs and results
docs.text:
A simulation in SIMANFOR generates a comprehensive set of dasometric outputs describing the quantitative, qualitative, and structural evolution of the forest stand over time. These results are compiled into Excel workbooks (.xlsx), with an individual workbook produced for each simulated plot.

This guide details the internal architecture of the output sheets, the definition of each variable category, the quality control checks applied by the simulation engine, and the practical interpretation of tree dynamics and commercial bucking.

docs.title: Table of contents
docs.text:
• Structure of the output workbook
  • Downloadable sample files and data
  • Resumen (Summary) sheet: biometric synthesis and management balance
  • Diagnóstico (Diagnosis) sheet: quality control and biological ranges
  • Parcelas (Plots) sheet: stand-level biometric dynamics
  • Árboles (Trees) sheet: individual-tree dynamics and tracking

docs.title: Structure of the output workbook
docs.text:
Upon simulation completion, the platform packages all outputs into a compressed archive (.zip). Extracting this archive yields one spreadsheet file per simulated plot, formatted according to a standardized naming pattern:

<codigo_escenario>_Inventory_<id_inventario>__Plot_<id_parcela>.xlsx

For instance, in the walkthrough simulation presented in this web documentation, the scenario code is generated automatically, the inventory code inside the dataset is Del_Rio_et_al_2006, and the file contains five plots with ID_Parcela 12, 15, 18, 21, and 24. The extracted .zip content is shown below:

Each workbook is structured into four dedicated worksheets:

  1. Resumen (Summary): Executive sheet featuring scenario and model metadata alongside a synoptic balance of stand metrics before, during, and after each silvicultural intervention.
  2. Diagnóstico (Diagnosis): Technical report validating compatibility between inventory inputs, model requirements, and simulated executions.
  3. Parcelas (Plots): Longitudinal table tracking the temporal trajectory of aggregate stand-level variables (density, basal area, volume, biomass, carbon, and diverse indices) across each scenario step.
  4. Árboles (Trees): Granular record at individual tree level, tracking tree vital status, biometric dimensions, and commercial log product assortment.

docs.title: Downloadable sample files and data
docs.text:
To facilitate exploration while reviewing this guide, you can download the actual files generated by our reference simulation for Pinus sylvestris (Scots pine) projected with the IBEROPS (calibrated) model over 20 years with a 20% basal area thinning from below:

  • Complete results package (ZIP containing 5 sample plots)

You can also download individual plot workbooks directly to inspect them in your preferred spreadsheet software:

  • Plot 12 results workbook (XLSX)
  • Plot 15 results workbook (XLSX)
  • Plot 18 results workbook (XLSX)
  • Plot 21 results workbook (XLSX)
  • Plot 24 results workbook (XLSX)

docs.title: Resumen (Summary) sheet: biometric synthesis and management balance
docs.text: The Resumen sheet delivers an executive overview suitable for technical reports, management plans, and rapid assessments:

docs.title: Simulation metadata block
docs.text:
The header rows (rows 1 to 4) record execution traceability details:

  • Inventario (Inventory) and Parcela (Plot): Baseline inventory source file and numerical identifier of the analyzed sample plot.
  • Modelo (Model): Official catalog model name (e.g., IBEROPS (calibrado)) and a summary of its ecological scope.
  • Documentación (Documentation): Direct link to the official technical documentation for the model, in this case the IBEROPS (calibrated) model.
  • Fecha (Date) and Cita (Citation): Timestamp of simulation execution and formal recommended citation strings for acknowledging both the specific forest model and the SIMANFOR platform in scientific literature and technical projects.

docs.title: Silvicultural intervention balance
docs.text:
Starting from row 6, the sheet displays a comparative table organized into three horizontal blocks evaluating the quantitative impact of each scheduled silvicultural intervention:

Dasometric block Included variables Forestry interpretation Masa antes de la corta (Pre-harvest stand) Age (years), $Ho$ (m), $N$ (trees/ha), $dg$ (cm), $G$ ($\text{m}^2/\text{ha}$), $V$ ($\text{m}^3/\text{ha}$) Stand biometric condition at each projection step immediately preceding silvicultural treatment. Masa extraída (Harvested timber) $N$ (trees/ha), $dg$ (cm), $G$ ($\text{m}^2/\text{ha}$), $V$ ($\text{m}^3/\text{ha}$), % $N$, % $G$, % $V$ Absolute and relative quantification of timber removed during thinnings or final harvest operations. Masa después de la corta (Post-harvest stand) $N$ (trees/ha), $dg$ (cm), $G$ ($\text{m}^2/\text{ha}$), $V$ ($\text{m}^3/\text{ha}$) Residual growing stock remaining in the stand following intervention, serving as the starting baseline for the subsequent growth cycle.

docs.title: Diagnóstico (Diagnosis) sheet: quality control and biological ranges
docs.text: The simulation engine incorporates an automated auditing module that monitors the mathematical consistency and biological plausibility of predictions at each step:

docs.title: Quality traffic light
docs.text:
In the report header, SIMANFOR summarizes the overall execution status using three severity tiers:

  • 🟢 Óptimo (Optimal): The simulation completed without warnings. All stand and tree variables remained within the empirical bounds and biological validity range of the model calibration.
  • 🟡 Aviso (Warning): The simulation completed calculations, but specific metrics (e.g., tree slenderness, mortality rates, or periodic diameter increments) slightly exceeded typical biological expectations. Flagged entries should be reviewed in the diagnostic table below.
  • 🔴 Error: The simulation encountered a severe numerical discontinuity, a structural mismatch between inventory data and model requirements, or an invalid parameter that compromises projection accuracy.

docs.title: Diagnostic issues table
docs.text:
When warnings or notifications are recorded, the table breaks down each issue across ten diagnostic columns:

  1. Severidad (Severity): Impact level (WARNING or ERROR).
  2. Código (Code): Internal rule identifier triggered during execution.
  3. Categoría (Category): Biological or dasometric module involved (mortality, diameter growth, height-diameter allometry, volume, or biomass).
  4. Paso (Step): Chronological scenario step index where the condition was flagged.
  5. Operación (Operation): Operation type (Ejecución or Corta).
  6. Árbol (Tree): Target tree identifier (blank for stand-level evaluations).
  7. Variable: Name of the audited metric (e.g., dbh, h, or ratio_esbeltez).
  8. Valor observado (Observed value): Numerical value computed by the engine.
  9. Rango admisible (Admissible range): Valid domain defined by the model (tolerable minimum and maximum thresholds).
  10. Mensaje (Message): Explanatory description of the anomaly and recommended interpretation.

docs.title: Parcelas (Plots) sheet: stand-level biometric dynamics
docs.text: The Parcelas sheet tracks the complete stand-level chronology across time, presenting each stage of the prescription as a distinct row:

docs.title: Control and timeline columns
docs.text:
The initial columns define the operational context and temporal framework:

  • Accion: Action type recorded in the row:
    • Carga Inicial: Raw baseline measurements loaded from the input inventory file.
    • Inicialización: Values calibrated following assignment of derived baseline metrics by the model (e.g., heights calculated via $h/d$ equations, initial volumes, and biomass components).
    • Ejecución: Stand state upon concluding a projection period (natural growth).
    • Corta: Immediate post-intervention stand state following a thinning or harvest operation.
  • Tiempo_acumulado_simulacion: Cumulative years elapsed since the beginning of the simulation.
  • Tiempo_proyectado_accion: Duration of the current operational step (e.g., 5 for growth projections and 0 for instantaneous cutting steps).
  • Tipo_de_corta, Criterio_de_corta, Intensidad_de_corta: Harvest specifications configured for the step (e.g., Corta por lo bajo, Área basimétrica, and 20%).
  • ID_Inventario, ID_Parcela, ID_especie: Unique identifiers for inventory dataset, sample plot, and species code.
  • Anho and T: Calendar year and stand physiological age for the given step.

docs.title: Stand dasometric variables
docs.text:
Subsequent columns present aggregate biometric metrics:

  • Stand density ($N$): Live trees per hectare (N), natural mortality (N_muerto), harvested trees (N_corta), and recruitment (N_incorporado).
  • Basal area ($G$): Total cross-sectional area at 1.30 m in $\text{m}^2/\text{ha}$ (G), alongside harvested basal area (G_corta) and natural mortality (G_muerta).
  • Representative diameters: Arithmetic mean diameter (dbh_medio), quadratic mean diameter (dg), dominant diameter (Do, mean of the 100 thickest trees per hectare), and bounds (dbh_minimo, dbh_maximo).
  • Heights: Mean stand height (h_media) and Assmann dominant height (Ho, mean of the 100 tallest trees per hectare).

For mathematical definitions, refer to the variables: dimensions and productivity catalogs.

docs.title: Timber volume and commercial product assortment
docs.text:
Merchantable timber volume is quantified at plot scale:

  • Global volumes: Over-bark stem volume (V_con_corteza), under-bark stem volume (V_sin_corteza), and bark volume (V_de_corteza), all expressed in $\text{m}^3/\text{ha}$.
  • Commercial log bucking assortment: When the model includes industrial product taper tariffs, volume is classified by commercial log specifications:
    • V_desenrollo and V_chapa: Large-diameter high-value veneer logs.
    • V_sierra_gruesa, V_sierra, and V_sierra_canter: Sawtimber of varied dimensional classes.
    • V_postes and V_estacas: Poles and agricultural stakes.
    • V_trituracion: Small-diameter roundwood for pulp or particleboard panels.

Not all forest models support commercial assortment bucking, as species-specific stem profile equations are required. Where unsupported, these columns are omitted from results. Review the variables: wood products guide and the models catalog to check feature availability per model.

docs.title: Biomass fractions and carbon balance
docs.text:
SIMANFOR estimates dry matter biomass using species-specific allometric systems (in tons of dry matter per hectare, $\text{t}/\text{ha}$):

  • Above-ground fractions: Stem wood (WS), thick branches with diameter $> 7\ \text{cm}$ (WSW), medium branches between $2$ and $7\ \text{cm}$ (WB2_7), fine branches with needles/leaves (WTBL), and total above-ground biomass (WA).
  • Below-ground fraction: Coarse and fine root biomass (WR).
  • Total biomass (WT): Integral biomass across all compartments ($WT = WA + WR$).
  • Carbon stocks: Elemental carbon stored in each tree component (Carbono_tronco, Carbono_ramas, Carbono_aereo, Carbono_raices, and Carbono_total), derived by applying species-specific dry matter carbon conversion factors.

Further details are available in variables: biomass and variables: carbon, with model compatibility noted in the models catalog.

docs.title: Stand structure, competition, and biodiversity
docs.text:
The final columns capture advanced stand structural and ecological parameters:

  • Competition and relative density: Reineke stand density index (SDI), relative density ratio to biological maximum (r_(SDI)), Hart-Becking spacing index under square and triangular spacing (Indice_Hart, Indice_Hart_tresbolillo), and stand slenderness ratio (Esbeltez = $\frac{Hm}{dg} \times 100$).
  • Structural and species diversity: Coefficients of variation for diameter (CV_dbh) and height (CV_altura), Shannon indices for dimensional stratification, and classic taxonomic diversity metrics (Shannon-Weaver, Simpson, Margalef, and Pielou).

docs.title: Non-timber products and additional variables
docs.text: Certain models calculate stand-level non-timber forest products (such as pine nuts in Pinus pinea, cork in Quercus suber, resin in Pinus pinaster, or mushroom yields; see variables: non-timber resources). Additionally, depending on the inventory inputs or selected model, columns related to climate, LiDAR metrics, or site station characteristics may appear. When not supported by the model, these columns are omitted.

docs.title: Árboles (Trees) sheet: individual-tree dynamics and tracking
docs.text: For individual-tree models, the Árboles sheet records the step-by-step trajectory of every measured tree within the plot:

docs.title: Identification and vital status
docs.text:
Each row captures an individual tree record at a specific simulation step:

  • ID_Arbol: Unique numerical identifier assigned to each tree in the initial inventory, ensuring continuity throughout projections.
  • id_especie and nombre_especie: National Forest Inventory species code (21) and binomial scientific name (Pinus sylvestris).
  • estado: Vital or management status of the tree at that step:
    • vivo: Live tree growing actively and continuing into the next projection interval.
    • cortado: Tree harvested in its entirety during a thinning or harvest step (100% of its expansion factor removed). Does not appear in subsequent projection intervals.
    • parcialmente_cortado: Tree whose expansion factor was partially harvested during a percentage-based intervention. The extracted fraction is logged at that step, and the residual fraction remains in the stand as vivo.
    • muerto: Tree that died from natural mortality (self-thinning competition or senescence) during the projection period.
    • incorporado: Tree recruited from natural regeneration that attained the minimum inventory diameter threshold (ingrowth).
    • nuevo: Tree assigned a newly generated identification code upon entering the simulated stand via natural regeneration.
  • factor_expansion: Tree expansion factor ($expan$), representing the statistical weight (trees per hectare) embodied by the measured sample tree. See its definition here.

docs.title: Allometry, growth, and competition
docs.text:
• Dimensions and increments: Diameter at breast height (dbh), total height (altura), individual basal area (g, g_ha), and their respective periodic increments (dbh_i, g_i, altura_i, v_i, wt_i) evaluated by the model equations (see variables: dimensions).
  • Competition and crown metrics: Basal area of larger trees (bal), split by intra- and inter-specific pressure (bal_intrasp, bal_intersp), alongside crown parameters (hcb, cr, lcw, hlcw) reflecting vertical competitive suppression (see variables: competition).

docs.title: Individual timber products and carbon
docs.text: Mirroring the stand-level sheet but calculated for individual stems, columns detail tree-level volumes (v_con_corteza, v_ha), commercial log bucking categories (v_chapa, v_sierra_gruesa, v_sierra, v_trituracion), biomass components (ws, wb, wa, wr, wt), and elemental carbon fixation (carbono_total).

docs.title: Non-timber forest products
docs.text: While not applicable to this Scots pine reference run, specialized models calculate non-timber forest products (such as stone pine cone and nut production in Pinus pinea, cork yields in Quercus suber, resin tapping in Pinus pinaster, or edible mushroom yields in mycological models). When the active model implements these equations, the corresponding columns are automatically included in both the plot and tree sheets; otherwise, they are omitted to streamline output files. Consult the variables: non-timber resources guide and the models catalog.

docs.title: Management scenarios on the web platform
docs.text:
A silvicultural scenario in SIMANFOR is the chronological sequence of events describing the productive cycle of a forest stand. It combines growth projections over time with cutting operations (thinnings or cleanings) scheduled according to technical criteria.

Users manage and run simulations through the web platform (simanfor.es) without writing code or manually editing configuration files. From the browser, you can link an inventory, associate it with a forest growth model, configure the silvicultural treatments, launch the simulation, and download the results.

docs.title: Table of contents
docs.text:
• General workflow
  • Prerequisites on the web platform
  • Creating a new scenario
  • Configuring management steps
    • Growth projections
    • Cuttings and silvicultural treatments
  • Multi-stand simulations and age bounds
  • Control panel and table options
  • Contents of the results bundle

docs.title: General workflow
docs.text:
The diagram below outlines the four primary phases of scenario management on the web platform:

  1. Prerequisites: confirm the inventory is uploaded and check the recommended projection time step in the model datasheet.
  2. Scenario design: sequentially add the required projections and cuttings.
  3. Panel and actions: verify the steps under details and start the simulation run.
  4. Results: download the compressed file containing the Excel workbooks (one file per plot).

docs.title: Prerequisites on the web platform
docs.text: Before creating a scenario in SIMANFOR web, prepare two items:

docs.title: 1. Inventory uploaded to the user account
docs.text:
The inventory contains the initial forest measurements. Upload it via the Inventories section in the sidebar as an Excel file (.xlsx).

The workbook must contain at least two sheets with standard names:

  • Parcelas: defines stand or sample plot characteristics (plot_id, area, age, or site index when available).
  • Árboles (or PiesMayores): contains tree-level measurements for individual-tree models (tree_id, dbh, height, species code, and expansion factor expan).

Uploaded inventories remain private to your user account for simulation use. For further details on inventory formats, refer to the Inventories documentation.

docs.title: 2. Selecting and reviewing the forest model
docs.text:
The Models section lists all available models on the platform. Before designing a scenario, review the technical documentation in the Models index to check three aspects:

  • Compatibility: verify that the model covers the tree species and geographic origin of the plots.
  • Required data level: determine whether the model is tree-level (requiring diameter and height for each tree) or stand-level (operating on aggregate variables such as basal area and density).
  • Recommended projection time: this parameter is essential. Growth and survival submodels are calibrated using permanent sample plots remeasured at specific intervals (typically 5 or 10 years). To maintain dasometric and mathematical consistency, projections in the scenario should use this interval as their base time step.

docs.title: Creating a new scenario
docs.text:
Once the inventory is ready and the model chosen, start from the sidebar:

  1. Open the Scenarios section.
  2. Click the top button Add new scenario.
  3. Complete the initial form fields:
    • Name: enter a descriptive title to identify the run in the table (for example, Pinus pinaster - Low thinning 20%).
    • Initial inventory: select the file uploaded earlier. Use the brown selector button to switch files if needed.
    • Projection model: select the target forest model.

Confirming these settings automatically configures data loading and model initialization, leaving the builder ready for silvicultural steps.

docs.title: Configuring management steps
docs.text: Build the scenario by adding operations chronologically with the Add next step button. Each step represents an event in the forest stand and belongs to one of two categories:

docs.title: Growth projections
docs.text:
A projection advances the simulation clock. During this step, the engine evaluates diameter increment, height growth, natural mortality, and ingrowth.

To schedule a projection, click Apply Projection and configure its variables:

  • Execution period (time): the number of years the stand will grow. This should match the recommended projection interval from the model documentation (for example, 5 years). To simulate 20 years without intermediate interventions, schedule 4 consecutive 5-year projections rather than a single 20-year step. The model interface suggests recommended projection periods on the left.
  • Age bounds (min_age and max_age): optional filtering parameters. They restrict growth execution to plots whose age falls within the specified range. If a plot falls outside, the projection step is skipped for that plot. These bounds allow running one scenario across plots with different initial ages while keeping biological behavior consistent.

docs.title: Cuttings and silvicultural treatments
docs.text:
A cutting extracts trees to manage stand competition and produce timber. Unlike projections, cuttings do not advance biological time; they represent instantaneous events.

To schedule a cut, click Apply Cutting and set the following parameters:

  • Harvest model: dropdown list of cutting types. Available options depend on the model level:
    • Individual-tree models: thinning from below, thinning from above, systematic thinning, cuttings with future crop tree retention, or species-directed cuts in mixed stands. For complete explanations, see the Harvest models documentation.
    • Stand-level models: stand-level reductions that decrease total basal area or volume without selecting individual stems.
  • Execution period (time): keep this set to 0. Cuttings are instantaneous events. A value above 0 causes the engine to calculate growth concurrently during tree removal.
  • Cutting criterion (type): the metric used to calculate removals:
    • Density (Number of trees / Density): percentage of trees per hectare removed.
    • Basal area (Basal area): percentage of basal area removed ($G$ in m²/ha).
    • Volume (Volume): percentage of standing timber volume removed ($V$ in m³/ha).
  • Cutting intensity (percent): exact percentage of the chosen criterion to harvest (from 1 to 100).
  • Age bounds (min_age and max_age): age window within which the cutting applies. These bounds are useful when dealing with unevenly aged stands, such as applying a thinning only to mature plots while skipping younger ones.

Simulating semi-systematic thinnings

The web interface does not provide a single button for semi-systematic thinnings, but you can reproduce them accurately by chaining two consecutive steps at the same age:

  1. A systematic cutting representing rack or corridor opening (for example, harvesting 1 out of 5 rows, equivalent to a 20 % systematic cut).
  2. A subsequent thinning from below applied to the remaining trees between corridors, using the desired residual percentage.

If you make a mistake while setting up a step, remove it using the Remove step button. Once the schedule is complete, click Accept to save the scenario.

docs.title: Multi-stand simulations and age bounds
docs.text: Inventories often contain multiple stands with different initial ages (for instance, plots aged 20, 32, 41, and 47 years). Rather than creating a separate scenario for each stand, SIMANFOR applies a single scenario across all plots using operational bounds (min_age and max_age).

docs.title: Engine evaluation rule
docs.text:
When processing a plot at any step, the simulator verifies whether the current plot age satisfies:

$$\text{min_age} \le \text{Plot age} \le \text{max_age}$$

  • If the age is within the interval, the operation (cutting or projection) executes normally.
  • If the age falls outside, the operation is skipped for that plot, and the engine moves directly to the next step.

docs.title: Setting tolerance margins
docs.text: Because plot ages in field inventories rarely align with exact multiples of the projection cycle (such as a 32-year-old stand under a 5-year step), set a tolerance window of 2 to 3 years above and below the target age.

docs.title: Practical example: silvicultural schedule for Pinus pinaster
docs.text:
Consider an 80-year rotation for Pinus pinaster with the following silvicultural schedule:

  • Age 20: initial cleaning (if density exceeds 1,500 trees/ha).
  • Age 40: first thinning (38 % removal via semi-systematic thinning).
  • Age 50: second thinning from below (40 % stem removal).
  • Age 65: third thinning from below (27 % stem removal).
  • Age 80: rotation age.

Translating this prescription into a multi-stand scenario with a 5-year step yields the following schedule:

Step Operation Type / Treatment Criterion and intensity Standard age Programmed bounds (min_age - max_age) 1 Projection 5-year growth - 20 to 25 17 to 23 2 Projection 5-year growth - 25 to 30 22 to 27 3 Projection 5-year growth - 30 to 35 27 to 32 4 Projection 5-year growth - 35 to 40 32 to 37 5 Cutting Systematic (racks) $N = 19\,\%$ 40 37 to 42 6 Cutting Thinning from below $N = 24\,\%$ 40 37 to 42 7 Projection 5-year growth - 40 to 45 37 to 42 8 Projection 5-year growth - 45 to 50 42 to 47 9 Cutting Thinning from below $N = 40\,\%$ 50 47 to 52 10 Projection 5-year growth - 50 to 55 47 to 52 11 Projection 5-year growth - 55 to 60 52 to 57 12 Projection 5-year growth - 60 to 65 57 to 62 13 Cutting Thinning from below $N = 27\,\%$ 65 62 to 67 14 Projection 5-year growth - 65 to 70 62 to 67 15 Projection 5-year growth - 70 to 75 67 to 72 16 Projection 5-year growth - 75 to 80 72 to 77

Final rotation harvest

Do not schedule a 100 % clearcut at the end of the rotation (age 80). If a total cut is applied, all standing inventory values drop to zero in the output file. Project the stand up to rotation age to inspect the accumulated standing stock before the final harvest.

docs.title: Control panel and table options
docs.text:
After saving, the scenario appears in the main table of the Scenarios section:

The table displays identification columns (NAME), owner (AUTHOR), attached inventory (INVENTORY), selected model (PROJECTION MODEL), simulation status (STATUS), and action buttons (ACTIONS):

Button Operational function When to use Details Opens a modal listing all configured steps in order. Includes the green Run button at the bottom. Review scheduled steps and age bounds, and launch the simulation. Edit Reopens the scenario builder with editable fields. Modify parameters, add intermediate steps, or delete operations before running. Delete Permanently removes the scenario and its settings from your account. Clean up old tests or discarded runs. Results Activates once status changes to FINISHED. Opens the download modal for the compressed .zip package. Retrieve output workbooks after calculation finishes on the server.

docs.title: Lifecycle and simulation execution
docs.text:
1. NOT_STARTED status: the scenario is saved but has not been sent to the simulation server.
  2. Launch: click Details and then click the green Run button. The system packages internal configurations and transfers them to the engine.
  1. RUNNING status: calculations are underway on the compute cluster. Processing time depends on plot count, stem density, and the number of projection steps. Refresh the web page manually (using F5 or the reload button) to check whether calculations have finished.
  2. FINISHED status: the engine has completed calculations, and output files are packaged. The green Results button activates in the table.

Occasional connection hiccups during execution

If the status does not update after refreshing with F5, or if network connectivity dropped momentarily, reopen the Details modal and click Run again. The platform will resend the simulation request.

docs.title: Contents of the results bundle
docs.text:
Clicking Results and confirming download retrieves a .zip archive containing one Excel workbook (.xlsx) per processed inventory plot.

Each Excel file contains the following sheets:

  • Summary: a yield table summarizing overall stand metrics across the simulation. Shows initial standing stock, total harvested volumes, and net accumulated growth.
  • Diagnostico (or Report): a diagnostic validation sheet flagging whether any dasometric metric (such as height, slenderness, or density) exceeded the biological range of the model.
  • Parcelas (or Plots): detailed time series of stand-level variables at each node (initial, before cut, after cut, and projections). Includes density ($N$), basal area ($G$), dominant height ($Ho$), quadratic mean diameter ($Dg$), standing volume ($V$), biomass fractions, and carbon stock.
  • Árboles (or Trees): individual stem records across time for tree-level models, tracking diameter, height, biomass, and stem status (alive, dead, cut, or ingrowth).

These files can be examined directly in spreadsheet software or imported into statistical packages like R or Python to plot growth trajectories and compare silvicultural alternatives. For a comprehensive guide to sheet structures and dasometric interpretation of output variables, see the Simulation results and outputs guide.

docs.title: Practical examples and scenario comparison
docs.text:
The design of silvicultural scenarios allows contrasting different management regimes on the same forest stand to evaluate their impact on growth, timber yield, and stand ecological stability.

This guide details the parametrization of two contrasting silvicultural alternatives applied to the same starting stand:

  1. Control scenario (no intervention): the stand evolves naturally without silvicultural interventions, driven solely by biological growth and competition-induced natural mortality.
  2. Technical management scenario based on scientific literature: implementation of a reference silvicultural regime for Pinus pinaster afforestation stands in Castilla y León for site quality 21, taken from the Management manual for afforestation stands of Pinus pinaster Ait., Pinus sylvestris L. and Pinus nigra Arn. in Castilla y León (del Río et al., 2006).

docs.title: Table of contents
docs.text:
• Starting forest stand
  • Reference silvicultural schedule
  • Design of the control scenario
  • Design of the technical management scenario
    • Intervention at 25 years: first thinning
    • Intervention at 35 years: second thinning
    • Intervention at 45 years: third thinning
    • Intervention at 55 years: fourth thinning
    • Reaching rotation age
  • Table of operations in SIMANFOR web
  • Comparison of results between alternatives
  • Bibliographic references

docs.title: Starting forest stand
docs.text:
The study case is located in an afforestation stand of maritime pine (Pinus pinaster Ait.) in Castilla y León, characterized by a high site quality defined by a site index of 21 meters at the reference age of 50 years ($SI = 21\text{ m}$).

The dasometric variables of the stand at the start of the simulation (age 25 years, prior to the first intervention) are as follows:

  • Stand age ($E$ or $\text{Age}$): 25 years
  • Stand density ($N$): 1,500 stems/ha
  • Dominant height ($Ho$): 12.1 m
  • Quadratic mean diameter ($Dg$): 14.6 cm
  • Basal area ($G$): 25.2 m²/ha
  • Total volume over bark ($V$): 127.8 m³/ha

To replicate this exercise directly on the SIMANFOR web platform, the pre-formatted Excel inventory file containing the two mandatory sheets (Parcelas and PiesMayores) is available for download:

Download sample initial inventory (inventario_ppinaster_cyl_calidad21.xlsx)

Starting from this same initial inventory loaded onto the web platform, two independent management scenarios are configured to evaluate stand performance across a 65-year rotation.

docs.title: Reference silvicultural schedule
docs.text:
The silvicultural schedule proposed by del Río et al. (2006) for Pinus pinaster at site quality 21 establishes the following technical timeline:

  • 10 to 15 years: if initial density exceeds 1,500 stems/ha, juvenile thinning (pre-commercial clearing) combined with low pruning.
  • 25 years: first semi-systematic thinning with low thinning between rows.
  • 33 years: second thinning from below.
  • 42 years: third thinning from below.
  • 52 years: fourth thinning from below.
  • 65 years: final harvest (rotation age).

Stand biological age and simulation starting point

All timeline references in the silvicultural regime refer to stand biological age, not to elapsed years since simulation start.

Since our sample inventory starts at 25 years with 1,500 stems/ha, the simulation begins directly at that milestone. Consequently, modeling earlier juvenile treatments between ages 10 and 15 is unnecessary, as the initial stand is already positioned for its first commercial thinning.

docs.title: Design of the control scenario
docs.text: The control scenario (commonly referred to as No intervention, natural succession, or walk-away management) simulates spontaneous stand development in the absence of any harvesting or silvicultural treatment.

docs.title: Dasometric logic of the control
docs.text:
Because density remains unmanaged, the stand undergoes intense intra-specific competition for light, soil moisture, and nutrients:

  • Individual tree diameter increment slows down substantially due to continuous crown closure.
  • The height-to-diameter ratio (slenderness index, $H/Dg$) rises, increasing stand vulnerability to windthrow and snow damage.
  • Natural mortality through self-thinning increases, accumulating standing and fallen deadwood that raises forest fire propagation risk.

docs.title: Configuration on SIMANFOR web
docs.text:
On the web platform, this scenario is set up as follows:

  1. Create a new scenario named Pinus pinaster - Control no intervencion.
  2. Select the uploaded inventory and the forest model. In this example, IBEROPT calibrated is selected provisionally, as the specific stand dynamic model from del Río et al. (2006) is not yet implemented in the simulator.
  3. Schedule consecutive growth projections using the model standard time step (5 years) until reaching rotation age (65 years):
    • 8 consecutive projections with time = 5 (40 years of biological advance: $25 + 40 = 65\text{ years}$).
  4. Do not add any operation of type Aplicar Corta.

docs.title: TODO: Implement in the simulator the dynamic stand model by Del Río et al. (2006) for Pinus pinaster in Castilla y León and update this example replacing IBEROPT with the new model.
Design of the technical management scenario
docs.text:
The second scenario translates technical prescriptions from scientific literature into specific simulator operations. Each intervention requires specifying the dasometric target variable ($N$, $G$, or $V$) and the exact harvesting intensity.

In forest growth models within SIMANFOR, projections advance in discrete 5-year cycles (time = 5). To adapt theoretical intervention ages (25, 33, 42, 52, and 65 years) to standard 5-year intervals, thinnings are scheduled at the closest 5-year milestones: 25, 35, 45, 55, and 65 years. Exactly two 5-year projection cycles (10 years of growth) elapse between consecutive thinning events.

docs.title: Intervention at 25 years: first thinning
docs.text:
At age 25, reference prescription values are:

  • Pre-thinning stand: $N = 1,500\text{ stems/ha}$, $G = 25.2\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}$, $V = 127.8\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.
  • Extracted volume and trees: $N = 550\text{ stems/ha}$, $V = 38.7\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.
  • Residual stand: $N = 950\text{ stems/ha}$, $G = 17.7\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}$, $V = 89.1\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.

Total extraction intensity relative to stand density is:

$$\text{Total intensity} = \left(\frac{550}{1,500}\right) \cdot 100 = 36.7\,\%$$

Because the prescription calls for a semi-systematic thinning (combining row extraction with selective thinning from below between rows), it is configured in SIMANFOR via two consecutive steps at simulation start (execution time = 0):

  1. Step 1: Systematic cutting (skid trail opening):
  2. Model: Corta sistemática
  3. Criterion: Densidad
  4. Intensity: opening 1 row every 5 lines ($\approx 20\,\%$ systematic removal). This removes 300 stems/ha ($1,500 \cdot 0.20 = 300$), leaving 1,200 stems/ha.
  5. Step 2: Thinning from below (selection between rows):
  6. Model: Corta por lo bajo
  7. Criterion: Densidad
  8. Intensity: 250 stems/ha remain to be extracted ($550 - 300 = 250$) out of the 1,200 remaining trees: $$\text{Intensity from below} = \left(\frac{250}{1,200}\right) \cdot 100 = 20.8\,\%$$

This approach extracts exactly the targeted 550 stems/ha while maintaining the prescribed semi-systematic spatial structure.

docs.title: Intervention at 35 years: second thinning
docs.text:
Following the first thinning, the stand grows for 10 years through two consecutive 5-year projections to reach 35 years of biological age (practical adaptation of the 33-year literature milestone).

At this age, target values are:

  • Pre-thinning stand: $N = 950\text{ stems/ha}$, $G = 34.6\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}$, $V = 224.2\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.
  • Extracted trees: $N = 350\text{ stems/ha}$, $V = 63.7\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.
  • Residual stand: $N = 600\text{ stems/ha}$, $G = 25.0\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}$, $V = 160.4\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.

A thinning step from below is scheduled at execution time 0:

  • Harvest model: Corta por lo bajo
  • Execution time: 0
  • Criterion and intensity:
  • By density ($N$): $(350 / 950) \cdot 100 = 36.8\,\%$
  • (Alternatively, by basal area: $((34.6 - 25.0) / 34.6) \cdot 100 = 27.7\,\%$, or by volume: $(63.7 / 224.2) \cdot 100 = 28.4\,\%$)
  • Age bounds: min_age = 33, max_age = 37.

docs.title: Intervention at 45 years: third thinning
docs.text:
The stand is projected across two additional 5-year cycles (10 accumulated years) from age 35 to age 45 (adaptation of the 42-year milestone).

At age 45, literature values indicate:

  • Pre-thinning stand: $N = 600\text{ stems/ha}$, $G = 40.7\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}$, $V = 313.6\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.
  • Extracted trees: $N = 200\text{ stems/ha}$, $V = 88.3\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.
  • Residual stand: $N = 400\text{ stems/ha}$, $G = 29.4\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}$, $V = 225.3\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.

The following thinning step is scheduled:

  • Harvest model: Corta por lo bajo
  • Execution time: 0
  • Intensity based on density ($N$): $$\text{Intensity} = \left(\frac{200}{600}\right) \cdot 100 = 33.3\,\%$$ (Alternatively, on basal area: $27.8\,\%$ of $G$, or on volume: $28.2\,\%$ of $V$).
  • Age bounds: min_age = 43, max_age = 47.

docs.title: Intervention at 55 years: fourth thinning
docs.text:
The stand is projected once again over 10 years (two 5-year projections) from age 45 to age 55 (adaptation of the 52-year milestone).

At age 55, target values are:

  • Pre-thinning stand: $N = 400\text{ stems/ha}$, $G = 43.9\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}$, $V = 383.0\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.
  • Extracted trees: $N = 125\text{ stems/ha}$, $V = 103.3\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.
  • Residual stand: $N = 275\text{ stems/ha}$, $G = 32.3\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}$, $V = 279.7\text{ m}^3/\text{ha}$.

The final commercial thinning is configured:

  • Harvest model: Corta por lo bajo
  • Execution time: 0
  • Intensity based on density ($N$): $$\text{Intensity} = \left(\frac{125}{400}\right) \cdot 100 = 31.3\,\%$$ (Or $26.4\,\%$ on $G$, or $27.0\,\%$ on $V$).
  • Age bounds: min_age = 53, max_age = 57.

docs.title: Reaching rotation age
docs.text:
From age 55 to age 65, the final 10 years of rotation unfold via two consecutive 5-year projections. The 275 selected crop trees per hectare reach the final rotation age of 65 years.

At age 65, the stand accumulates the following final standing inventory:

  • Stand density ($N$): 275 stems/ha
  • Quadratic mean diameter ($Dg$): 45.9 cm
  • Dominant height ($Ho$): 23.9 m
  • Basal area ($G$): 45.5 m²/ha
  • Final standing volume over bark ($V$): 439.0 m³/ha

Do not schedule a 100 % clearcut at rotation age

As explained in the general scenarios guide, do not schedule a 100 % final cut at age 65. If a clearcut is applied, the Excel output workbook will report zero standing stock at the final node. The simulation must end on the final projection so that the harvestable stock can be evaluated in the Summary and Plots sheets.

docs.title: Table of operations in SIMANFOR web
docs.text:
The following table summarizes the complete 13-step chronological sequence entered into the web interface for the managed scenario, where all projections advance in 5-year steps (time = 5):

Step Web operation Main parameters Age bounds (min_age - max_age) Silvicultural objective 1 Aplicar Corta Systematic, $N = 20.0\,\%$, time = 0 23 - 27 Skid trail opening (age 25) 2 Aplicar Corta From below, $N = 20.8\,\%$, time = 0 23 - 27 Selection between rows (age 25) 3 Aplicar Proyección time = 5 25 - 31 Growth from 25 to 30 years 4 Aplicar Proyección time = 5 30 - 36 Growth from 30 to 35 years 5 Aplicar Corta From below, $N = 36.8\,\%$, time = 0 33 - 37 2nd thinning: reduction to 600 stems/ha (age 35) 6 Aplicar Proyección time = 5 35 - 41 Growth from 35 to 40 years 7 Aplicar Proyección time = 5 40 - 46 Growth from 40 to 45 years 8 Aplicar Corta From below, $N = 33.3\,\%$, time = 0 43 - 47 3rd thinning: reduction to 400 stems/ha (age 45) 9 Aplicar Proyección time = 5 45 - 51 Growth from 45 to 50 years 10 Aplicar Proyección time = 5 50 - 56 Growth from 50 to 55 years 11 Aplicar Corta From below, $N = 31.3\,\%$, time = 0 53 - 57 4th thinning: reduction to 275 stems/ha (age 55) 12 Aplicar Proyección time = 5 55 - 61 Growth from 55 to 60 years 13 Aplicar Proyección time = 5 60 - 66 Final growth to rotation age (age 65)

Use of age bounds (min_age and max_age)

Defining an age range using min_age and max_age is only necessary when the uploaded inventory contains multiple plots with heterogeneous ages. In that case, age bounds act as a conditional filter so that a thinning or treatment triggers only on stands whose current age falls within the specified window.

When the inventory consists of a single plot (as in this sample exercise) or multiple even-aged plots sharing the same initial age, configuring these fields is optional, as operations execute sequentially step by step in the scheduled chronological order.

docs.title: Comparison of results between alternatives
docs.text:
When downloading the Excel workbooks from both simulations and inspecting the Summary and Plots sheets, results demonstrate two completely distinct silvicultural trajectories:

Dasometric variable at rotation (65 years) Scenario 1: Control (no intervention) Scenario 2: Technical management regime Residual density ($N$) High (reduced only by self-thinning) 275 stems/ha (regulated density) Quadratic mean diameter ($Dg$) Low (growth stagnation through competition) 45.9 cm (large high-value timber) Thinning extracted volume ($\sum V_{\text{cortas}}$) 0 m³/ha 294.0 m³/ha ($38.7 + 63.7 + 88.3 + 103.3$) Final standing volume ($V_{\text{final}}$) Variable (high proportion of slender/dead stems) 439.0 m³/ha (premium sawtimber) Total volumetric yield Lower merchantable yield 733.0 m³/ha ($294.0 + 439.0$) Fire and pest vulnerability High (fuel load accumulation and crown continuity) Low (horizontal discontinuity and vigorous crowns) Slenderness coefficient ($H/Dg$) High (slender stems, lower stability against snow) Balanced (sturdy stems with greater taper)

docs.title: Technical conclusions
docs.text:
1. Growth concentration effect: The four commercial thinnings do not reduce cumulative stand volume; rather, they channel available light, soil water, and nutrients into the 275 crop trees, achieving a quadratic mean diameter of 45.9 cm at rotation.
  2. Intermediate timber revenue: The managed scenario provides 294 m³/ha of merchantable timber across four separate harvest events, generating regular financial returns throughout the rotation.
  3. Stand resilience: In the unmanaged control, elevated stocking levels produce slender trees prone to wind and snow damage, while heavy suppression mortality increases ground fuel loads. Active silviculture enhances structural stability and adaptive capacity against environmental disturbances.
