docs.title: General variables catalog
docs.text:
This section contains the comprehensive and unified dictionary of all variables used across the SIMANFOR platform. These variables cover both initial inventory metrics and those calculated by forest models and generated in output files.

Quick variable search

To instantly locate any variable by its descriptive name, output symbol or abbreviation, or accepted inventory synonym, use the search bar located in the upper-right corner of the screen (or press s or f).

docs.title: Information levels
docs.text:
In SIMANFOR, variables are structured primarily into two hierarchical levels:

  • Plot-level variables: Describe overall stand, plot, or inventory characteristics per unit area (frequently scaled per hectare, such as density in trees/ha or basal area in m²/ha).
  • Tree-level variables: Record measurements and estimates of individual inventoried trees (diameter at breast height, total height, unit volume, biomass fractions).

docs.title: Conventions and standards
docs.text:
• Standardized units: All units are explicitly stated in lowercase (e.g., t/ha for stand biomass and carbon, kg for individual tree biomass and carbon, m3/ha and dm3 for volumes, cm for diameters, m for heights, - for dimensionless indices, and ratio for proportions between 0 and 1).
  • Output labels and symbols: The bold name is the official descriptive name and the column header produced in simulator output files. For variables with a standard mensurational symbol or abbreviation (such as N for density or G for basal area), it is shown in parentheses beside the name: Density (N), which corresponds to the header in output files.
  • Accepted names in inventory: The simulator flexibly and case-insensitively accepts common synonyms (aliases) when importing inventories from Excel, CSV, or JSON formats, automatically including the Spanish denomination.
  • Multi-species variables: To perform stand calculations by species, some variables are presented broken down by species by adding the numerical suffix of the corresponding species (Species_SP1_name, Species_SP2_name, Species_SP3_name).
  • Dynamic management variables: Silvicultural interventions and demographic events incorporate standardized prefixes: _corta / _harvest (removals from thinning or felling), _muerto / _dead (natural mortality), and _incorporado / _ingrowth (ingrowth, considering trees of inventoriable size with diameter at breast height >= 7.5 cm and not seedlings from natural regeneration).

docs.title: Interpretation of variable entries
docs.text: Each catalog entry systematically describes variable attributes to simplify identification both during field inventory preparation and when analyzing simulation output files.

docs.title: Structure of each entry
docs.text:
• Name and output symbol: Official descriptive name in bold. If a standard technical symbol or abbreviation exists, it appears in parentheses: Name (Symbol). This symbol (or the name itself if no specific abbreviation exists) is the exact column header produced in simulator output files (Excel or CSV).
  • Data type: Technical value format (text, decimal, integer).
  • Units: Standardized measurement unit (dimensionless, cm, m, m2/ha, trees/ha, t/ha, ratio).
  • Multi-species tag: For variables broken down by species, indicates available numerical suffixes (multi-species: sp1, sp2, sp3).
  • Description: Technical or mensurational definition of the parameter.
  • Accepted names in inventory: Synonyms and column headers flexibly and case-insensitively accepted when importing inventories in Excel, CSV, or JSON (including the Spanish denomination).
  • Simulation breakdown: In multi-species variables, explanatory callout listing the specific disaggregated columns produced in outputs.
  • References: In modeled or empirical variables, scientific citations with direct DOI links to publications containing implemented equations.

docs.title: 1. Inventory and basic setup variable
docs.text:
Variables intended to uniquely identify plots or trees in input inventory files:

  • ID_inventory — text  •  dimensionless

    Unique identifier of the forest inventory.

    Accepted names in inventory: id_inventario, inventory, id_inventory, inventario, ID_inventario

Interpretation: Since it lacks an abbreviated symbol in parentheses, the output column header will be ID_inventory (or Inventory_ID). In field inventory files uploaded to SIMANFOR, any of the listed names is recognized.

docs.title: 2. Mensurational variable with standard symbol and multi-species breakdown
docs.text:
Stand metrics calculated both globally and broken down for each target species:

  • Density (N) — decimal  •  trees/ha  •  multi-species: sp1, sp2, sp3

    Number of trees per hectare.

    Accepted names in inventory: n, pies_ha, densidad, density, Densidad

    Simulation breakdown: This variable is automatically expanded for each target stand species (Density_SP1, Density_SP2, Density_SP3).

Interpretation: In downloaded simulation results, overall stand density is reported under column N, while species-specific densities appear under columns N_sp1, N_sp2, and N_sp3.

docs.title: 3. Estimated variable with scientific references
docs.text:
Variables calculated using biological, allometric, or empirical models implemented in the simulator:

  • N_cones (N_cones) — decimal  •  cones/ha/year

    Mean annual pine cone production per hectare.

    References:

    • Calama & Montero (2006). Cone and seed production from stone pine (Pinus pinea L.) stands in Central Range (Spain). European Journal of Forest Research. (DOI:10.1007/s10342-005-0100-8)
    • Calama et al. (2008). An empirical ecological-type model for predicting stone pine (Pinus pinea L.) cone production in the Northern Plateau (Spain). Forest Ecology and Management. (DOI:10.1016/j.foreco.2007.09.079)

Interpretation: The output column will be named N_cones. The entry links directly to reference scientific papers containing implemented equations.

docs.title: 4. Dynamic management and demographic variables
docs.text:
Variables quantifying changes between simulation cycles resulting from thinnings, natural mortality, or ingrowth:

  • Volume_harvest (V_harvest) — decimal  •  m3/ha

    Merchantable timber volume removed during thinning or felling operations in the period.

Interpretation: Silvicultural event variables incorporate standardized prefixes or suffixes: _corta / _harvest or _cut (removals), _muerto / _dead (natural mortality), and _incorporado / _ingrowth (new recruit trees).

docs.title: Inventory identification and characteristics
docs.text: Variables designed to uniquely identify inventories, sample plots, and individual trees within the simulator, as well as qualitative parameters of form, quality, and health status.

docs.title: Plot-level variables
docs.text:
• ID_inventory — text  •  dimensionless

    Unique identifier of the forest inventory.

    Accepted names in inventory: id_inventario, inventory, id_inventory, inventario

  • ID_plot — text  •  dimensionless

    Unique plot identifier.

    Accepted names in inventory: id_parcela, plot, parcela, id_plot, id_parc

  • Country — text  •  dimensionless

    Country where the plot is located.

    Accepted names in inventory: Pais

  • Province — text  •  dimensionless

    Administrative province where the plot is located. It is recommended to provide the official two-digit numeric code from the Spanish National Statistics Institute (INE) or the official name. This variable is required to load the volume equations and coefficients of the Spanish National Forest Inventory (SNFI).

    Accepted names in inventory: Province, provincia, cod_prov, id_provincia

  • Municipality — text  •  dimensionless

    Municipality where the plot is located.

    Accepted names in inventory: Municipio

  • Biogeographic_region — text  •  dimensionless

    Biogeographic region of the stand (e.g. Mediterranean, Atlantic).

    Accepted names in inventory: Region_biogeografica

  • Forest — text  •  dimensionless

    Name of the forest estate.

    Accepted names in inventory: Monte

  • Study_area — text  •  dimensionless

    Identifier or designation of the study area.

    Accepted names in inventory: Zona_estudio

  • Stand_origin — text  •  dimensionless

    Origin of the forest stand (natural or plantation/artificial).

    Accepted names in inventory: Origen_masa

  • Natural_regeneration — integer  •  dimensionless

    Presence or density class of natural regeneration in the plot. Used in the Romania stand model and takes values from 1 to 8.

    Accepted names in inventory: Regeneracion_natural

  • ID_species_{num} — integer  •  dimensionless  •  multi-species: sp1, sp2, sp3

    Identifier code of species {num} according to the Spanish National Forest Inventory (SNFI) standard. Inventories accept both the official numeric SNFI code and the official scientific name (e.g. "Pinus sylvestris"), resolved bidirectionally by the simulator. Common or vernacular names are not allowed.

    Accepted names in inventory: {sp}_id, id_{sp}, species_{num}_id, especie_{num}_id, id_sp{num}

    Simulation breakdown: This variable is automatically expanded for each target stand species (ID_species_SP1, ID_species_SP2, ID_species_SP3).

  • Name_species_{num} — text  •  dimensionless  •  multi-species: sp1, sp2, sp3

    Formatted scientific name of species {num} present in the plot. It can be provided directly as a binomial Latin name or inferred automatically from the numeric SNFI code. Vernacular names are not allowed.

    Accepted names in inventory: {sp}_name, name_{sp}, species_{num}_name, especie_{num}_nombre, nombre_{sp}

    Simulation breakdown: This variable is automatically expanded for each target stand species (Name_species_SP1, Name_species_SP2, Name_species_SP3).

  • Clone_species_{num} — text  •  dimensionless  •  multi-species: sp1, sp2, sp3

    Clone identifier for species {num}. Currently used in Populus_sp_stand__NE model with fields like I214, MC or LA.

    Simulation breakdown: This variable is automatically expanded for each target stand species (Clone_species_SP1, Clone_species_SP2, Clone_species_SP3).

  • Species_composition — text  •  dimensionless

    Description of species mixture or proportions in the plot.

    Accepted names in inventory: Composicion_especies

  • Year — integer  •  dimensionless

    Year associated with the rest of the state variables.

    Accepted names in inventory: ano, Año, anio, year, Anho

docs.title: Tree-level variables
docs.text:
• id_inventory — text  •  dimensionless

    Identifier of the inventory the tree belongs to.

    Accepted names in inventory: id_inventario, inventory, id_inventory, inventario

  • id_plot — text  •  dimensionless

    Identifier of the plot the tree belongs to.

    Accepted names in inventory: id_parcela, plot, parcela, id_plot, id_parc

  • id_tree — text  •  dimensionless

    Unique tree identifier within the plot.

    Accepted names in inventory: id_arbol, tree, id_tree, arbol

  • species_id — integer  •  dimensionless

    Numeric or identifier code of the tree species according to the Spanish National Forest Inventory (SNFI) or equivalent. The inventory species column accepts both the numeric SNFI code and the official scientific name (e.g. "Pinus sylvestris"), with automatic bidirectional resolution. Common or vernacular names are not allowed.

    Accepted names in inventory: species, id_especie, especie, sp, cod_esp

  • species_name — text  •  dimensionless

    Scientific or canonical name of the tree species. Can be specified directly in the inventory or automatically inferred from the SNFI code. Vernacular names are not allowed.

In growth models (Aguirre et al., 2026), it modifies annual diameter and height increment for species with special uses or conditions (such as resin tapping in Pinus pinaster or cork debarking in Quercus suber; default 1 = not resinated/not debarked, 0 = no special parameter).

  • distance — decimal  •  m

    Horizontal distance from the plot center to the tree.

    Accepted names in inventory: distancia

docs.title: Stand structure and canopy metrics
docs.text: Horizontal and vertical stand structure metrics (coefficients of variation, structural diversity indices, slenderness) and crown mensuration variables at plot and tree levels.

docs.title: Plot-level variables
docs.text:
• Slenderness (S_mean) — decimal  •  dimensionless  •  multi-species: sp1, sp2, sp3

    Mean stand slenderness coefficient. Ratio of mean tree height to mean diameter at breast height.

    Accepted names in inventory: Esbeltez

    Simulation breakdown: This variable is automatically expanded for each target stand species (Slenderness_SP1, Slenderness_SP2, Slenderness_SP3).

  • Dominant_slenderness (S_dom) — decimal  •  dimensionless  •  multi-species: sp1, sp2, sp3

    Dominant stand slenderness coefficient. Ratio of dominant height to dominant diameter.

    Accepted names in inventory: Esbeltez_dominante

    Simulation breakdown: This variable is automatically expanded for each target stand species (Dominant_slenderness_SP1, Dominant_slenderness_SP2, Dominant_slenderness_SP3).

  • Mean_crown_d (dc_mean) — decimal  •  m  •  multi-species: sp1, sp2

    Mean tree crown diameter in the plot.

    Accepted names in inventory: d_medio_copa

    Simulation breakdown: This variable is automatically expanded for each target stand species (Mean_crown_d_SP1, Mean_crown_d_SP2).

  • Do_crown — decimal  •  m  •  multi-species: sp1, sp2

    Dominant crown diameter of the stand.

    Accepted names in inventory: Do_copa

    Simulation breakdown: This variable is automatically expanded for each target stand species (Do_crown_SP1, Do_crown_SP2).

  • Canopy_cover (FCC) — decimal  •  %  •  multi-species: sp1, sp2

    Canopy cover fraction. Percentage of ground covered by the vertical projection of tree crowns.

    Accepted names in inventory: FCC

    Simulation breakdown: This variable is automatically expanded for each target stand species (Canopy_cover_SP1, Canopy_cover_SP2).

  • Canopy_vol (V_canopy) — decimal  •  m3/ha  •  multi-species: sp1, sp2

    Apparent volume occupied by tree crowns per hectare.

    Accepted names in inventory: Volumen_copa

    Simulation breakdown: This variable is automatically expanded for each target stand species (Canopy_vol_SP1, Canopy_vol_SP2).

  • CCF — decimal  •  %

    Stand crown competition factor (CCF). Percentage of area occupied by potential crowns of open-grown trees.

    Accepted names in inventory: CCF

  • CV_dbh — decimal  •  %

    Coefficient of variation of the diameter at breast height distribution (%). Ratio of the standard deviation to the mean of dbh values in the plot.

    Accepted names in inventory: CV_dbh

    Reference: Varga et al. (2005). Tree-size diversity in progression of stand development in Douglas-fir forests. Forest Ecology and Management.

  • CV_height (CV_h) — decimal  •  %

    Coefficient of variation of the height distribution (%). Ratio of the standard deviation to the mean of height values in the plot.

    Accepted names in inventory: CV_altura

    Reference: Varga et al. (2005). Tree-size diversity in progression of stand development in Douglas-fir forests. Forest Ecology and Management.

  • Shannon_dbh_index — decimal  •  dimensionless

    Shannon-Weaver Diversity Index applied to dbh distribution in the plot, using 5 cm diameter classes. This positive index usually ranges from 0.5 to 5, with typical values between 2 and 3. Values below 2 are considered low in diversity, while values above 3 indicate high species diversity.

    Accepted names in inventory: Indice_Shannon_dbh

    References:

    • Varga et al. (2005). Tree-size diversity in progression of stand development in Douglas-fir forests. Forest Ecology and Management.
    • Omoro et al. (2010). Tree biomass and soil carbon stocks in Taita Hills, Kenya. African Journal of Ecology.
    • Moreno-Fernández et al. (2025). Structural diversity indices in managed forests.

  • Shannon_h_index (Shannon_h) — decimal  •  dimensionless

    Shannon-Weaver Diversity Index applied to height distribution in the plot, using 2.5 m height classes. This positive index usually ranges from 0.5 to 5, with typical values between 2 and 3. Values below 2 are considered low in diversity, while values above 3 indicate high species diversity.

    Accepted names in inventory: Indice_Shannon_h

    References:

    • Varga et al. (2005). Tree-size diversity in progression of stand development in Douglas-fir forests. Forest Ecology and Management.
    • Omoro et al. (2010). Tree biomass and soil carbon stocks in Taita Hills, Kenya. African Journal of Ecology.
    • Moreno-Fernández et al. (2025). Structural diversity indices in managed forests.

  • Structural_diversity_index_dbh — decimal  •  dimensionless

    Stand structural diversity index based on the sum of square roots of tree dbh differences (Barbeito et al., 2009).

    Accepted names in inventory: Indice_diversidad_estructural_dbh

    References:

    • Moreno-Fernández et al. (2025). Structural diversity indices in managed forests.
    • Barbeito (2009). Natural regeneration dynamics of Pinus sylvestris L. in Central Spain.

  • Structural_diversity_index_height — decimal  •  dimensionless

    Stand structural diversity index based on the sum of square roots of tree height differences (Barbeito et al., 2009).

    Accepted names in inventory: Indice_diversidad_estructural_altura

    References:

    • Moreno-Fernández et al. (2025). Structural diversity indices in managed forests.
    • Barbeito (2009). Natural regeneration dynamics of Pinus sylvestris L. in Central Spain.

docs.title: Biodiversity and deadwood indices
docs.text: Structural and species diversity indices (Shannon, Simpson, Margalef, Pielou) alongside standing and downed coarse woody debris indicators for ecological assessment.

docs.title: Plot-level variables
docs.text:
• Shannon_index — decimal  •  dimensionless

    Shannon-Weaver Diversity Index (H). This positive index typically ranges from 0.5 to 5 in natural ecosystems, with most values between 2 and 3. Values below 2 are low in diversity, while values above 3 indicate high species diversity..

    Accepted names in inventory: Indice_Shannon

    Reference: Omoro et al. (2010). Tree biomass and soil carbon stocks in Taita Hills, Kenya. African Journal of Ecology.

  • Simpson_index — decimal  •  dimensionless

    Modified Simpson Diversity Index. This index ranges from 0 to 1, where higher values indicate greater diversity, representing the probability that two randomly selected individuals belong to different species.

    Accepted names in inventory: Indice_Simpson

    Reference: Simpson (1949). Measurement of Diversity. Nature.

  • Margalef_index — decimal  •  dimensionless

    Margalef Species Diversity Index. Values below 2 usually indicate low biodiversity (human-impacted ecosystems), while values above 5 suggest high biodiversity.

    Accepted names in inventory: Indice_Margalef

    Reference: Ulanowicz (2001). Information theory in ecology. Computers & Chemistry.

  • Pielou_index — decimal  •  dimensionless

    Pielou Evenness Index. It measures the proportion of observed diversity relative to the maximum possible diversity, ranging from 0 to 1, with 1 indicating equal abundance of all species and 0 indicating no uniformity.

    Accepted names in inventory: Indice_Pielou

    Reference: Bray & Curtis (1957). An Ordination of the Upland Forest Communities of Southern Wisconsin. Ecological Monographs.

  • DBI_G — decimal  •  dimensionless

    Deadwood Biodiversity Index developed by CESEFOR, assessing deadwood quantity in stands with a quadratic mean diameter (dg) ≥ 17.5 cm. If the deadwood basal area exceeds 6% of trees with a dbh of 17.5 cm or larger, the deadwood status is classified as positive (1); otherwise, it is insufficient (0). Not applied to stands with a dg < 17.5 cm (-).

    Accepted names in inventory: DBI_G

  • DBI_V — decimal  •  dimensionless

    Deadwood index calculated on volume (CESEFOR methodology).

    Accepted names in inventory: DBI_V

docs.title: Climatic variables and bioclimatic indices
docs.text: Meteorological precipitation, seasonal temperature parameters, and climatic indices (such as Martonne index) required by climate-sensitive growth models.

docs.title: Plot-level variables
docs.text:
• Mean_annual_precipitation (RAIN_AA) — decimal  •  mm

    Mean annual cumulative precipitation of the plot. Used as a general climatic descriptor and in calculating De Martonne aridity index.

    Accepted names in inventory: Precipitacion_media_anual

  • Mean_annual_temperature (TEMP_MA) — decimal  •  °c

    Mean annual temperature of the plot. Used as a general climatic descriptor and in calculating De Martonne aridity index.

    Accepted names in inventory: Temperatura_media_anual

  • September_precipitation (RAIN_SEP) — decimal  •  mm

    Mean monthly precipitation for September. Used in mushroom yield estimation in Ppinaster_m_stand__iberian_peninsula and IBEROPT (Herrero et al., 2019), and mycorrhizal fungal diversity in Cladanifer_stand__zam (Hernández-Rodríguez et al., 2015).

    Accepted names in inventory: Precipitacion_septiembre

  • September_mean_temperature (TEMP_SEP) — decimal  •  °c

    Mean monthly temperature for September. Used in mushroom yield estimation in Ppinaster_m_stand__iberian_peninsula and IBEROPT (Herrero et al., 2019).

    Accepted names in inventory: Temperatura_media_de_septiembre

  • November_precipitation (RAIN_NOV) — decimal  •  mm

    Mean monthly precipitation for November. Used in mushroom yield estimation in Ppinaster_m_stand__iberian_peninsula and IBEROPT (Herrero et al., 2019).

    Accepted names in inventory: Precipitacion_noviembre

  • November_mean_temperature (TEMP_NOV) — decimal  •  °c

    Mean monthly temperature for November. Used in mushroom yield estimation in Ppinaster_m_stand__iberian_peninsula and IBEROPT (Herrero et al., 2019).

    Accepted names in inventory: Temperatura_media_de_noviembre

  • Martonne (M) — decimal  •  dimensionless

    De Martonne aridity index (P / (T + 10)). Used in the Mixed Models of Spain (mixed_models_Spain) to adjust diameter growth, survival, height-diameter curves, and maximum stand density (year <= 2020).

    Accepted names in inventory: Martonne_2001_2020, Martonne_2001-2020, Martonne_index, Martonne

    Reference: Martonne (1926). L’indice d’aridité. Bulletin de l’Association de géographes français.

  • Martonne_2021-2040 (M_2020) — decimal  •  dimensionless

    De Martonne aridity index projected for 2021-2040. Used in mixed_models_Spain for climate projections in that year range.

    Accepted names in inventory: Martonne_2021-2040

    Reference: Martonne (1926). L’indice d’aridité. Bulletin de l’Association de géographes français.

  • Martonne_2041-2060 (M_2040) — decimal  •  dimensionless

    De Martonne aridity index projected for 2041-2060. Used in mixed_models_Spain for climate projections in that year range.

    Accepted names in inventory: Martonne_2041-2060

    Reference: Martonne (1926). L’indice d’aridité. Bulletin de l’Association de géographes français.

  • Martonne_2061-2080 (M_2060) — decimal  •  dimensionless

    De Martonne aridity index projected for 2061-2080. Used in mixed_models_Spain for climate projections in that year range.

    Accepted names in inventory: Martonne_2061-2080

    Reference: Martonne (1926). L’indice d’aridité. Bulletin de l’Association de géographes français.

  • Martonne_2081-2100 (M_2080) — decimal  •  dimensionless

    De Martonne aridity index projected for 2081-2100. Used in mixed_models_Spain for climate projections beyond 2080.

    Accepted names in inventory: Martonne_2081-2100

    Reference: Martonne (1926). L’indice d’aridité. Bulletin de l’Association de géographes français.

  • August_september_precipitation — decimal  •  mm

    Cumulative precipitation for August and September. Used in Cladanifer_stand__zam (Hernández-Rodríguez et al., 2015) to estimate mycorrhizal fungal diversity.

    Accepted names in inventory: Precipitacion_agosto_septiembre

  • September_october_minimum_temperature — decimal  •  °c

    Mean minimum temperature for September and October. Autumn climatic variable registered for shrubland mycology models (Cladanifer_stand__zam).

    Accepted names in inventory: Temperatura_minima_septiembre_octubre

  • October_november_minimum_temperature — decimal  •  °c

    Mean minimum temperature for October and November. Used in Cladanifer_stand__zam (Hernández-Rodríguez et al., 2015) to estimate saprotrophic fungal diversity.

    Accepted names in inventory: Temperatura_minima_octubre_noviembre

  • October_november_december_minimum_temperature — decimal  •  °c

    Mean minimum temperature from October to December. Used in Cladanifer_stand__zam (Hernández-Rodríguez et al., 2015) to estimate saprotrophic fungal diversity.

    Accepted names in inventory: Temperatura_minima_octubre_noviembre_diciembre

  • October_minimum_temperature — decimal  •  °c

    Monthly mean of daily minimum temperatures in October. Used in Cladanifer_stand__zam (Hernández-Rodríguez et al., 2015) to estimate mycorrhizal fungal yield.

    Accepted names in inventory: Temperatura_minima_octubre

  • Sum_mean_temperatures_september_october — decimal  •  °c

    Sum of mean monthly temperatures of September and October. Used in Cladanifer_stand__zam (Hernández-Rodríguez et al., 2015) to estimate Boletus edulis yield.

    Accepted names in inventory: Suma_temperaturas_medias_septiembre_octubre

  • Sum_minimum_temperatures_september_october — decimal  •  °c

    Sum of minimum temperatures of September and October. Used in Cladanifer_stand__zam (Hernández-Rodríguez et al., 2015) to calculate Boletus edulis yield and mycorrhizal diversity.

    Accepted names in inventory: Suma_temperaturas_minimas_septiembre_octubre

  • Sum_minimum_temperatures_october_november — decimal  •  °c

    Sum of minimum temperatures of October and November. Used in Cladanifer_stand__zam (Hernández-Rodríguez et al., 2015) to estimate saprotrophic fungal yield.

    Accepted names in inventory: Suma_temperaturas_minimas_octubre_noviembre

  • Sum_minimum_temperatures_september_december — decimal  •  °c

    Sum of minimum temperatures from September to December. Used in Cladanifer_stand__zam (Hernández-Rodríguez et al., 2015) to estimate saprotrophic fungal yield.

    Accepted names in inventory: Suma_temperaturas_minimas_septiembre_diciembre

  • Temperature_sum — decimal  •  °c

    Cumulative temperature thermal sum (April, May, and June 30-year mean). Used in the SiTree model (Antón-Fernández et al., 2016) as a thermal modifier for site index estimation.

    Accepted names in inventory: Suma_termica

  • Monthly_moisture_surplus — decimal  •  mm

    Monthly moisture surplus in June defined as the difference between 30-year mean precipitation and potential evapotranspiration. Used in the SiTree model (Antón-Fernández et al., 2016) as a moisture modifier for site index estimation.

docs.title: Canopy LiDAR metrics
docs.text: Statistical canopy metrics derived from airborne laser scanning point clouds (height percentiles, return density distributions, dispersion, and canopy cover) for remote sensing modeling.

docs.title: Plot-level variables
docs.text:
• ZPCUM1 — decimal  •  %

    Cumulative percentage of return in the 1st layer according to Wood et al. 2008 (see metrics named d1, d2, ...).

    Accepted names in inventory: ZPCUM1

    References:

    • Roussel (n.d.). R package "lidR": Airborne LiDAR Data Manipulation and Visualization for Forestry Applications. (Link)

docs.title: Access and first steps on the web platform
docs.text:
The SIMANFOR web platform (simanfor.es) allows simulating forest stand growth and testing management alternatives directly from the browser, without installing local software, setting up development environments, or managing operating system dependencies.

This guide outlines account registration, language configuration, and the overall navigation layout of the service.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Platform purpose and scope
  • Account registration and activation
  • Login and credential recovery
  • Language selection
  • General interface layout
  • Core workflow

docs.title: Platform purpose and scope
docs.text:
The cloud service is primarily intended for forest managers, environmental consultants, educators, and university students who need to simulate forest inventories and evaluate silvicultural interventions through an accessible graphical interface.

The web environment covers the complete simulation lifecycle:

  • Uploading forest inventory data in Excel format.
  • Selecting growth and yield models from the official catalog.
  • Visually designing silvicultural schedules with projection intervals and percentage-based thinnings.
  • Automatic processing on the remote compute server and downloading results in spreadsheets.

For large-scale batch processing across thousands of plots, integration into automated statistical workflows in R or Python, or developing and calibrating new forest models, refer to the platform execution pathways guide. That section details simulation scripts and high-performance computing deployment options.

docs.title: Account registration and activation
docs.text:
Access to the platform is free and open. To use the platform, you must create a user account:

  1. Go to simanfor.es.
  2. On the main landing screen, click on the Solicitud de Registro (or Sign up / Iniciar sesión / Registrar) button in the top right header.
  3. Complete the required fields in the registration form (user name, email address, password, and confirmation). In the Rol (Role) field, select the default option (Básico).
  4. After submitting the application, the SIMANFOR team will validate and accept the request to activate your user account, after which you can log in directly with your credentials.

docs.title: Login and credential recovery
docs.text:
Once your account has been registered, enter your username and password into the login form and click Iniciar sesión (or Login).

Credential management

Keep your credentials secure. If you forget your access password or encounter issues accessing your account, contact technical support at simanfor.forest@uva.es.

docs.title: Language selection
docs.text:
The web interface features multilingual support accessible at any time from the dropdown selector located in the top-right corner of the header:

Available languages:

  • Spanish (Español).
  • English.
  • Galician (Galego).
  • French (Français).
  • Portuguese (Português).
  • Vietnamese (Tiếng Việt).
  • Basque (Euskara).
  • Romanian (Rumâniascǎ).

Partial interface translations

Translation progress is ongoing. For languages where specific UI labels or system messages are not yet fully localized, text defaults to English.

docs.title: General interface layout
docs.text:
After logging in, you will access the main workspace. Primary navigation is organized in the left-hand sidebar menu across the following tabs:

  • Inventarios (Inventories): Section to upload, list, and inspect the Excel (.xlsx) files containing baseline biometric data for your plots or stands.
  • Modelos (Models): Informational catalog detailing the mathematical growth, mortality, and yield equations programmed in SIMANFOR. Allows reviewing target species, geographic coverage, and projection intervals. More details are available in the models catalog.
  • Escenarios (Scenarios): Central section for designing silvicultural prescriptions. Here you link an inventory, select a projection model, program interventions, and launch simulations.
  • Resultados (Results): History and access to data packages generated after running scenarios.
  • Ayuda (Help): Links to external resources and contact information for the development team.
  • Aviso Legal (Legal Notice): Link to the platform terms of service and legal notice.

docs.title: Core workflow
docs.text:
Every simulation on SIMANFOR web follows a logical sequence of four steps:

  1. Upload inventory: Load baseline field plots in Excel format (see Inventory management and upload).
  2. Define scenario: Select the forest model and schedule projection steps and thinning treatments (see Scenario design).
  3. Run: Launch the computation on the remote server and monitor execution progress.
  4. Download and analyze: Retrieve the .zip archive containing detailed Excel output workbooks for each plot (see Simulation execution and troubleshooting).

Translated using AI translation assistant.

docs.title: Forest inventory management and upload
docs.text:
A forest inventory provides the baseline biometric data required to initiate any simulation in SIMANFOR. It represents the state of one or multiple plots at a specific measurement year prior to projecting growth or applying silvicultural treatments.

This guide explains format requirements for the web platform, the step-by-step upload procedure, and critical privacy considerations.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• File format requirements
  • Uploading a new inventory
  • Upload form fields
  • Visibility and selection warning
  • Reviewing the uploaded inventory

docs.title: File format requirements
docs.text:
While the SIMANFOR simulation engine locally supports .xlsx, .csv, and .json files when executed via scripts, the web platform exclusively accepts files in Excel (.xlsx) format.

The workbook must comply with standard SIMANFOR structural conventions:

  • Parcelas (Plots) sheet: Specifies general metadata for each sampled plot or stand (plot_id, area, and optional attributes such as stand age, site quality, or coordinates).
  • Árboles or PiesMayores (Trees) sheet: Records tree-level measurements for individual-tree models (tree_id, dbh, height, species code, and individual expansion factor expan).

For downloadable templates, normalized variable identifiers, and official Spanish National Forest Inventory (NFI) species codes, refer to the technical guide on inventory preparation.

Excel sheet verification

Ensure that worksheet names match Parcelas and PiesMayores exactly (respecting capitalization), that no blank intermediary rows exist, and that decimal notations (periods or commas) remain consistent throughout the file.

docs.title: Uploading a new inventory
docs.text:
To upload your inventory data to the web platform:

  1. Log in to simanfor.es.
  2. In the top navigation bar, click on the Inventarios tab.
  3. Above the inventories table, click the Subir Nuevo (or Upload New) button.

A modal dialog will open displaying the import form.

docs.title: Upload form fields
docs.text:
Complete the required fields in the dialog box:

  • Nombre (Name): Enter a descriptive name to easily identify the plot set later on (for example, inventario ejemplo or Pinus_sylvestris_Soria_2024).
  • Año de creación (Creation year): Specify the year when field measurements were collected (for example, 2026). This value is informational and does not constrain calculations, but facilitates temporal tracking across subsequent steps.
  • Tipo (Type): File format to import (defaults to Excel).
  • Inventario público (Public inventory): Checkbox to share the file with other platform users (unchecked by default, keeping it private to your account).
  • Formato de inventario (Inventory format): Select the Simanfor radio button. The alternative Smartelo represents a complementary marteloscope module currently under development.
  • Fichero (File): Click the blue button to select and attach the .xlsx file from your local computer (for example, Psylvestris_CyL-datos_ejemplo.xlsx).

Once all fields are filled, click Aceptar to register the inventory on the platform:

docs.title: Visibility and selection warning
docs.text:
When an inventory is uploaded, the file is transferred to the web server and registered within your account.

Critical notice on the inventory selector

In the current version of the web platform, the inventory dropdown menu may occasionally display files uploaded by other users hosted on the same server.

Always select strictly your own inventory (identified by the exact name you assigned during upload). Selecting another user's file will cause the simulation to fail due to access permission restrictions and biological inconsistencies with the chosen model.

docs.title: Reviewing the uploaded inventory
docs.text:
Once the upload finishes, you will be redirected to the Inventarios table. You can verify that your record is correctly listed with its name, creation date, author, and format:

The platform assigns a unique internal numeric ID to your inventory. With this step completed, your dataset is ready to be linked to a forest growth model and configured within a management schedule in the Scenario design section.

Translated using AI translation assistant.

docs.title: Silvicultural scenario design and configuration
docs.text:
A scenario in SIMANFOR defines the technical management schedule that a forest stand undergoes over time. It consists of an ordered sequence of chronological operations: natural growth periods (projections) and silvicultural interventions (thinnings or final fellings).

This guide explains how to structure a scenario on the web platform, select an appropriate model, configure each operational step, and save the schedule for execution.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Scenario concept in SIMANFOR
  • Creating a new scenario
  • Linking baseline inventory and forest model
  • Configuring projection operations
  • Configuring harvest operations
  • Guided practical example
  • Saving and registering the scenario

docs.title: Scenario concept in SIMANFOR
docs.text:
The simulator requires knowing which growth and yield model governs the dynamics of the species and what management prescriptions will be applied chronologically.

On the web platform, scenario design is performed visually by linking two primary operational types:

  • Proyección (Projection): Advances the stand over time according to equations for diameter increment, height growth, natural mortality, and recruitment (when supported by the model).
  • Corta (Harvest): Implements tree removals based on a user-defined cutting type, selection criterion, and percentage-based extraction intensity.

docs.title: Creating a new scenario
docs.text:
To begin structuring a silvicultural prescription:

  1. Open the Escenarios tab in the main navigation menu.
  2. Click the Añadir nuevo escenario (or Add new scenario) button.

The scenarios table will be displayed. In the upper left area, click on the Añadir nuevo escenario button:

docs.title: Linking baseline inventory and forest model
docs.text:
In the new scenario configuration window, assign an identifiable name (for example, escenario ejemplo) and link your data and model:

  1. Click on Seleccionar Inventario. In the popup window, locate your uploaded inventory using the search box, select it, and click Seleccionar.
  2. Click on Seleccionar Modelo de Proyección. In the modal catalog, review the description to confirm target species and geographic scope (or check the models catalog), choose the model, and click Seleccionar.

Once linked, both components will be confirmed in the header of the form:

Inventory ownership verification

Always verify that the selected inventory file is the one you uploaded previously from your account (see Inventory management).

Before scheduling scenario steps, keep two foundational aspects in mind:

  1. Biometric baseline: Identify the initial stand age in your inventory or the year of field data collection. This enables scheduling silvicultural interventions that align with stand developmental stages and ensures chronological consistency across treatments.
  2. Intervention schedule: Plan the treatments to simulate, total temporal horizon, and specific management objectives (e.g., reducing density to foster diameter growth or determining rotation age). For detailed background, refer to the scenario guide and example scenarios.

docs.title: Configuring projection operations
docs.text:
To grow the forest stand over time, click the Aplicar Proyección button:

Complete the following fields:

  • Título y descripción (Title and description): Identifiers for this step (for example, title Proyección and description de 20 a 25 años). Providing clear notes is highly recommended to facilitate subsequent interpretation of outputs.
  • time (execution period): Number of years the stand should grow. This must match the valid interval supported by the selected model (displayed on the left side of the form).
  • min_age and max_age (optional): Age bounds for plots to which this projection applies. If your inventory contains a single plot or if the projection applies uniformly across all ages, leave these fields blank. Further details are in the scenario documentation.

Example view of a configured projection step:

Once configured, click Aceptar to conclude or Añadir nuevo paso to add another management action.

docs.title: Configuring harvest operations
docs.text:
To schedule a thinning or harvest intervention, click Aplicar Corta:

Configure the intervention parameters (see harvest models for background):

  • Título y descripción: Identify the treatment (for example, title Corta and description Clara por lo bajo del 20% en G).
  • time: For cutting operations, this value must strictly remain 0, as harvests are treated as instantaneous relative to multi-year growth intervals.
  • Tipo de corta (Thinning type):
    • Por lo bajo (from below): Preferentially extracts smaller or suppressed trees (traditional thinning to reduce competition and promote dominant strata).
    • Por lo alto (from above): Preferentially extracts codominant or dominant trees to open canopy gaps.
    • Sistemática (systematic): Removes trees uniformly across all diameter classes.
  • type (intervention criterion): Defines the reference biometric variable for intensity:
    • Densidad: Percentage of total tree density ($N$, stems/ha).
    • Área basimétrica: Percentage of total basal area ($G$, $\text{m}^2/\text{ha}$).
    • Volumen: Percentage of total commercial timber volume ($V$, $\text{m}^3/\text{ha}$).
  • percent (intensity): Percentage of stand stock to extract according to the selected criterion (for example, 20 for a 20% thinning).

Visual example of a configured cutting intervention:

docs.title: Guided practical example
docs.text:
The following prescription illustrates a standard schedule for a Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris) stand starting at age 20 with a 20-year simulation horizon, assessing stand conditions at age 40:

The schedule implements the following sequence of 5 operations:

  1. Step 1 (Projection from age 20 to 25): Initial 5-year growth step using the IBEROPS original model (time = 5).
  2. Step 2 (Harvest): Moderate thinning from below removing 20% of stand basal area (time = 0, type Por lo bajo, criterion Área basimétrica, intensity 20%).
  3. Step 3 (Projection from age 25 to 30): Post-intervention 5-year growth period (time = 5).
  4. Step 4 (Projection from age 30 to 35): Intermediate 5-year growth period (time = 5).
  5. Step 5 (Projection from age 35 to 40): Final 5-year growth period (time = 5), reaching rotation evaluation at age 40.

docs.title: Saving and registering the scenario
docs.text:
As you configure each intervention, click Añadir nuevo paso if you wish to append further steps to the management cycle.

Once the complete schedule is structured, review step ordering and click Aceptar (or Submit) at the bottom of the form. The scenario is saved to the database and appears in the Escenarios table with an assigned identifier and the status NOT_STARTED:

Your scenario is now ready for execution. Refer to the next chapter, Simulation execution and troubleshooting, to initiate calculations and download output packages.

docs.title: Simulation execution and troubleshooting
docs.text:
Once a silvicultural scenario is designed, numerical processing is transferred to the compute engine. Upon completion, detailed biometric outputs become available for download in a compressed archive.

This guide details the execution workflow, simulation states, output package structure, Excel sheet interpretation, and troubleshooting procedures for common issues.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Launching the simulation
  • Simulation state lifecycle
  • Downloading output packages
  • General structure of outputs
    • Summary sheet
    • Diagnosis sheet
    • Plots sheet
    • Trees sheet
  • Troubleshooting common issues
  • Technical support protocol

docs.title: Launching the simulation
docs.text:
To execute a configured scenario:

  1. Open the Escenarios tab in the main navigation menu.
  2. Locate your scenario in the table using its identifier name or associated metadata.
  3. In the scenario row under the actions column, click on Detalles (or Details).
  4. A popup modal displays a summary of all scheduled interventions. Confirm that the linked inventory, chosen model, and projection and thinning parameters are accurate.
  5. Click the green Ejecutar (or Run) button.

docs.title: Simulation state lifecycle
docs.text:
Each simulation tracks its execution state in the Estado (or Status) column of the Escenarios table:

  • NOT_STARTED: The scenario is registered and saved on the platform, but execution has not yet been initiated:

  • WAITING: The web server has dispatched the calculation job to the compute engine. The scenario is queued or processing on the server:

  • FINISHED: The simulation has completed successfully on the compute server. The green Resultados (Results) download button becomes enabled:

Execution time and browser refresh

Simulations for concise scenarios and single plots typically finish within seconds. If the status remains in WAITING longer than expected, refresh the webpage (press F5) to force an update of the service state.

docs.title: Downloading output packages
docs.text:
When the status column displays FINISHED:

  1. Click on the green Resultados button located in your scenario row.
  2. The Resultados del escenario modal will open, displaying the generated archive name (for example, 6adb0d0b5c49d04ec6347471.zip):

  1. Click Descargar archivo. The browser will automatically download the compressed .zip package.
  2. Extract the .zip archive on your computer to view the output workbooks.

One workbook per inventory plot

Inside the extracted archive you will find as many individual .xlsx workbooks as plots were present in your initial inventory. Each file is named automatically with the scenario ID, inventory name, and plot identifier:

docs.title: General structure of outputs
docs.text: Inside each .xlsx workbook, four dedicated worksheets record the complete biometric trajectory of the plot:

docs.title: Summary sheet
docs.text:
Provides a concise yield table summarizing the simulation:

  • Metadata block (header): Identifies inventory name, simulated plot (18), execution timestamp, forest model (IBEROPS calibrado in this example), an ecological summary, and direct links to the model documentation in SIMANFOR and bibliographic citations.
  • Yield table: Tracks stand development across each age (T), recording dominant height ($Ho$), stand metrics prior to harvest ($N$, $dg$, $G$, $V$), extracted volume and stems during thinnings ($N$, $dg$, $V$), and residual stand conditions after treatment ($N'$, $dg'$, $G'$, $V'$).

docs.title: Diagnosis sheet
docs.text:
Serves as the quality control report and biological validation check of the simulation:

  • Quality traffic light: A banner confirms biological model validity (e.g., ÓPTIMO: Simulación conforme a las especificaciones técnicas del modelo).
  • Issue tracking table: Categorizes any warnings or computational anomalies by severity, code, category, scenario step, operation, affected tree, diagnostic message, and suggested recommendations.
  • For comprehensive interpretation of diagnosis codes, refer to the output interpretation guide.

docs.title: Plots sheet
docs.text:
Contains comprehensive time-series measurements of all stand-level biometric variables calculated at each event:

  • Operation tracking: Details every scheduled action (Initial Load, Initialization, Execution steps, and Thinning treatments with type, criterion, and intensity).
  • Temporal and biometric metrics: Tracks cumulative and projected elapsed years, calendar year, stand age ($T$), density ($N$), quadratic mean diameter ($dg$), mean diameter ($dbh_media$), basal area ($G$), dominant height ($Ho$), timber volume assortments, and biomass components.
  • For column definitions, units, and formulas, consult the Stand variables catalog.

docs.title: Trees sheet
docs.text:
Provides individual-tree tracking for simulations driven by single-tree models:

  • Tree-level tracking (ID_Arbol): Tracks each measured tree across every intervention and growth period.
  • Biological state dynamics: Monitors tree condition (vivo for living, muerto for natural mortality, cortado for harvest removals, and nuevo / incorporado for recruitment and ingrowth).
  • Individual metrics: Records normal diameter ($dbh$), height, individual basal area ($g$), expansion factors, and intraspecific and interspecific competition indices.
  • Refer to the tree status dynamics guide for details regarding biological state transitions.

docs.title: Troubleshooting common issues
docs.text: If you encounter unexpected errors during simulation or download, review the following common causes:

docs.title: 1. The scenario remains stuck in WAITING status
docs.text:
• Cause: Browser-to-server polling lost connection, or there is a temporary queue on the compute server.
  • Solution: Press F5 (or reload the page) to refresh the table. If after several minutes the status remains in WAITING, open scenario details and click Ejecutar again.

docs.title: 2. An empty ZIP file (0 bytes) is downloaded
docs.text:
• Cause: The simulation engine aborted execution due to an incompatibility between input data and model specifications.
  • Recommended checks:
    1. Species and inventory: Verify that inventory species codes correspond exactly to species accepted by the selected model.
    2. Excel file structure: Confirm that your inventory contains no corrupted formulas, empty columns, or modified sheet names (they must be Parcelas and PiesMayores).
    3. Projection period (time): Check that the time parameter in projection steps is not blank and matches the model official step interval (e.g., 5 or 10 years).
    4. Harvest parameter (time): Ensure that thinning and felling operations strictly have time = 0.
    5. Excessive harvest intensity: Confirm that removal percentage does not exceed 100% of existing stand volume/density, and that stands meet minimum intervention ages.
    6. Incomplete scenario steps: Verify that your scenario contains no blank or unassigned operational steps.

docs.title: Technical support protocol
docs.text:
If after reviewing the checks above the simulation continues to fail or produces empty archives, contact the technical support team by email:

  • simanfor.forest@uva.es

To facilitate debugging, please include in your message:

  1. Your registered platform username.
  2. The scenario numerical ID displaying the issue.
  3. The .xlsx inventory file utilized.
  4. A brief description of the scheduled interventions.
